title: The legacy Notes organization inventory re-scans and re-hashes the whole organization source for every single intent it commits: O(n^2), on the event loop
trigger: Yes: Settings Manual Sync (and adoption resolve -> re-run) -> async worker on the loop -> ManualSyncControlService.run_once -> NotesOrganizationSyncService.advance_enrollment -> LegacyNotesOrganizationInventory.run() synchronously (notes_organization_sync_service.py:930-937). cost: The code shape was verified: about 10 scans, a canonical JSON and a SHA per iteration, and one commit per intent, all repeated per intent. The finder's pure-Python digest numbers (1.5 ms per iteration at S=500, 11.7 ms at S=3000, so 0.8 s and 35 s totals) are consistent with the shape, and the SQL scans and per-intent IMMEDIATE commits add to them. I did not re-measure.

Commit intents in batches (for example 200 per transaction, checkpoint after each batch). Index entries by key for _next_entry. Compute the link id once in add(). Run run() via asyncio.to_thread from advance_enrollment.
fix_notes: The lowest-risk first step is `await asyncio.to_thread(inventory.run, ...)` in advance_enrollment. That removes the freeze and leaves the O(n^2) cost in the background. ChaChaNotes connections are thread-local, so file-backed is fine, but a :memory: DB would break. Beware the proposed cheap fingerprints: PRAGMA data_version does not see writes from the same connection, total_changes is per-connection and is bumped by the inventory's own record_intent writes, and the link tables have no version column, so MAX(version) misses link churn. A correct fingerprint needs MAX(change_id) from sync_log or equivalent. Batching commits changes the per-intent after_commit or crash-resume granularity that tests pin. Indexing entries by key and computing the link id once are safe micro-fixes.

title: mutate_managed_folder_links scans the whole effective folder-link set twice per managed-owner mutation, inside the write transaction, just to diff one owner
trigger: Each lasting-notes-sync operation (external file create, edit or move, disconnect, restore) reaches reconcile_managed_memberships through the executor stages above, on a worker thread, and only when exactly one local-first Sync v2 profile exists. It fires about once per synced file event, and N times during an initial import of N files.
cost: Measured on an isolated synthetic in-memory SQLite with the real indexes. The plan is SCAN m USING INDEX idx_note_folder_memberships_active_note, a PK probe on folders and a covering PK probe on suppressions. One _effective_folder_links scan plus the set build costs 1.7 ms at 1k, 12.0 ms at 5k and 54 ms at 20k memberships. That is about the same as reconcile_managed's inherent owner read (1.9 ms, 11 ms and 87 ms). Per reconcile this adds roughly 24 ms at 5k and about 110 ms at 20k of extra write-lock hold on a worker thread. Any ChaChaNotes writer, including loop-side writes, waits behind it. It is not a loop freeze.
fix: Restrict both snapshots to the affected (folder_id, note_id) pairs: the owner's current memberships plus the `desired` set. A WHERE m.owner_id = ? OR (folder_id, note_id) IN (...) variant of the query is enough. Related but distinct: TASK-21132, the repository CTE anchoring on the whole closure.
fix_notes: The proposed fix (restrict the snapshots to the owner's pairs plus `desired`) is correct but gains little for the common single-root user: that candidate set is already about the whole table, and a per-pair check or large IN list can be slower than the index scan. The better approach is to compute the changed-pair set cheaply before mutating. Take the owner's active pairs (the idx_note_folder_memberships_managed_owner read that reconcile_managed already does) and diff them against `desired`, also counting owner_active flips; the result is usually 0-1 pairs per file event. Check only those pairs with the existing _folder_link_effective helper (notes_organization_sync_service.py:1711) before and after the mutation. Because effectiveness has union semantics, the 'before' check must run before the mutation, since another owner or a manual row can keep a pair effective. convert_owner_to_manual and remove_owner_memberships have no production callers, so the change could be limited to reconcile_managed. Tests need cases for a manual row plus a managed row on the same pair, and for suppressed pairs.

result = mutate(cursor=cursor, **arguments)
after = self._effective_folder_links(cursor)
for folder_id, note_id in sorted(before ^ after): ...
reason: The code is present on pin 840ed2ca58 as quoted. notes_organization_sync_service.py:301 and :303 call _effective_folder_links (:1726), which runs an unfiltered SELECT DISTINCT over note_folder_memberships JOIN note_folders with a correlated NOT EXISTS against the suppressions table, once before and once after the mutation. Both scans run inside notes_repository.db.transaction(), so the ChaChaNotes write lock is held throughout. Caller chain (full grep): the only live entry is NotesScopeService.reconcile_note_folder_owner_memberships (notes_scope_service.py:959-981), called from NotesSyncAuthority.reconcile_managed_memberships (notes_sync_authority.py:539-556). The executor calls that at notes_sync_executor.py:2708 (_disconnect_create), 2816 (_advance_create_restore), 3388 (_advance_new), 4061 (_advance) and 5204 (_reconcile_without_binding). convert_note_folder_owner_to_manual and remove_note_folder_owner_memberships have no production callers. This is NOT event-loop blocking: _run_folder_repository wraps the call in asyncio.to_thread (notes_scope_service.py:487-491), and the executor adds _joined_thread_call on top. The scan path is gated. The service must be wired (app.py:7234-7242 does this in production), and resolve_profile_scope(None) must find exactly one local-first Sync v2 profile; otherwise _profile returns None and mutate runs with no scans. There is no open task: TASK-21132 is the separate closure CTE, TASK-21129 is Done, and TASK-24307 (Done) introduced the effective-union semantics. Important nuance: `desired` is the WHOLE root's binding set (_desired_managed_memberships, executor:3606-3627), and reconcile_managed already reads every owner row, so each file event is inherently O(root size). For a single-root vault the two scans are a constant factor of about 2-3x on O(n) work already being done, not an asymptotic change. The gap only becomes asymptotic when there are many manual placements or several roots. During a bulk first sync of N files, N reconciles each pay the scans, adding to an already-quadratic total.

title: Backup and restore re-hash whole archives 9–13 times per operation; verify_sealed does 2 full passes per call
trigger: User-initiated backup (start_backup via the backup-create-start thread worker) and restore review/start (summary, preview_restore, start_restore via thread workers). Each restore phase calls verify_sealed again.
cost: Estimated, not re-measured here. The pass counts are verified from the code. At roughly 2 GB/s for hashlib SHA-256 on this machine class, a 5 GB profile costs about 15–30 s of extra hashing CPU plus 35–55 GB of extra reads. The per-chunk statvfs is about 80k calls per 5 GB, a few hundred ms, and minor.
fix: Hash during the copy in copy_capture_file and in acquire's input copy, and return the digest. For process-owned private staging files, detect changes by comparing the `_identity` fstat tuple (dev, ino, size, mtime_ns, ctime_ns, already captured) instead of re-hashing, keeping one authenticated hash per artifact. verify_sealed should do an identity check plus a manifest re-read, re-hashing only when the identity changed. Drop `_space` from _inspect's read loop. Pick ZIP_STORED for high-ratio members during the first package pass instead of re-packaging everything.
fix_notes: The repeated hashes are deliberate TOCTOU defences in the ADR-126 design (for example, verify_sealed's contract is to invalidate the preview if the completed bytes changed). Replacing them with an fstat identity tuple weakens that: mtime is settable with utime, and the change detector relies on ctime granularity. Treat that part as security-review territory, not low risk. Zero-risk wins first: (1) hash during copy_capture_file and return the digest, which saves 1N; (2) drop _space() from _inspect's read-only member loop, or check once up front. Medium risk: reuse acquire's digest of its private copy instead of the writer's pre- and post-acquire _hash passes. For plaintext, verified.digest equals the output digest; for encrypted, the ciphertext digest is carried in encrypted_source. Re-packaging for >100× members is rare and cannot be decided before compressing, so it is low value. The verify_sealed double-hash needs a design decision, not a mechanical change.

title: Raw-CLI output sanitizer walks every output character in Python, and keeps doing so after the preview and record caps are exhausted
trigger: Any raw-CLI command with large output (user `!cmd` or approved model raw_cli). The parent thread runs for as long as the command streams.
cost: Measured on a loaded machine: sanitizer 141 ms per 1 MiB; accumulator 155 ms per first MiB and 85 ms per MiB after both budgets are full, with still only 5 events emitted. The finder's 54 ms/MB is on the low side, so 100 MB of output means about 5-15 s of GIL-held CPU in the app process. The loop still gets 5 ms switch-interval slices, so this slows the UI rather than freezing it.
fix: In consume(): once the preview budget and the record budget are exhausted and truncation has been reported for that stream, only add len(payload) to _raw_bytes and return (skip decode and sanitize). In feed(): add a fast path: if state is 'text', no pending CR, and one precompiled regex finds no C0/C1/ESC/CR characters in the chunk, return the text unchanged at C speed.
fix_notes: The budget short-circuit in consume() is safe only once truncation has been reported for that stream (_reported_truncation), and _raw_bytes must still be incremented so total_bytes stays exact. The incremental decoder state can be abandoned once the budgets are gone, because finish() output is also discarded then. The regex fast path must also require self._state == 'text' and not _pending_cr at chunk entry, and it must treat \r, ESC, C0 and 0x7F-0x9F as slow-path triggers (\x9b/\x9d/\x9c fall in C1).
reason: raw_cli_executor.py:575 _StreamSanitizer.feed is a per-character Python state machine. _OutputAccumulator.consume (679) always runs decode plus feed, and _accept then runs _utf8_prefix, which encodes the whole text again twice and builds an f-string record, even after MAX_RAW_PREVIEW_BYTES (32 KiB) and the record budget are both exhausted. consume is called from the parent-side loop (line 1386), inside RawShellExecutor.execute, which runs in a thread worker in the TUI process, so it competes for the GIL with the Textual loop. The worker's _drain_pipe forwards every byte in 8 KiB chunks with no output cap, so the parent processes all output. No open task covers it.

title: web_fetch and robots checks build a new httpx.Client (fresh SSLContext) per call, even on a warm cache hit, and never pool connections

Optionally keep one module-level client per UA with trust_env=False and follow_redirects=False.

A module-level shared client must keep trust_env=False and follow_redirects=False, and it must be safe across threads (httpx.Client is), but a pooled keep-alive connection could reuse a socket to an IP validated on an earlier hop. The SSRF guard validates per hop via DNS, so reusing connections across calls needs care. Caching the SSLContext per verify setting in tls_trust is the lowest-risk win.

title: First Console paint synchronously constructs the agent runtime (AgentRunsDB + ChangeTurnTracker + bridge) on the event loop
trigger: Every app launch with the default Console tab: the first ChatScreen.compose_content builds the workspace context state, which constructs the bridge synchronously on the event loop before the first paint. It is paid once per app session, because the runtime is app-owned. It also happens on the first Console visit whenever Console is not the startup tab.
cost: Measured independently in an isolated scratch profile (deep path). AgentRunsDB cold create took 136 ms. Reopen took 60 ms when the path was already swept, and 99 ms with a 300-run x 40-step history when reconcile runs. Reconcile scales linearly with history, because every terminal step payload is JSON-parsed inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE. ChangeTurnTracker() took 33-35 ms per call, almost entirely in get_user_data_dir admission. Add the bridge import (~24 ms per the finder; TASK-22213 confirms the import is on the mount path), the constructor, one historical_snapshot DB read and the on_mount durable wake-mark read. Real total is roughly 110-200 ms on a shallower real profile, and more for heavy agent users. That exceeds the P0 threshold of ≳100 ms on boot.
fix: Make compose and on_mount non-constructing. Read only `runtime.agent_bridge` (the `_attached_run_log_bridge` pattern already in agent.py:1294). Render 'Agent: idle' or an empty fleet state when it is None, then schedule `_request_console_agent_fleet_sync()` once the bridge exists. Pre-build the bridge in deferred startup or right after first paint with `await asyncio.to_thread(runtime.ensure_activity_receipt_service)` plus off-loop construction of ChangeTurnTracker, or have ChangeTurnTracker resolve its data dir lazily at first snapshot. Move the `_claim_console_fleet_wake_marks` seed after that await.
fix_notes: 1. 'Not built yet' must be a state distinct from None. `_ensure_console_agent_bridge` returning None currently means 'no durable DB', which paints 'Agent: unavailable' and empty sub-agent counts. Compose readers need a pending/idle rendering, not the unavailable one. 2. At least four compose-path callers exist (workspace.py:4392, agent.py:1144, agent.py:2018, fleet claim), and about 20 _ensure_console_agent_bridge sites exist overall. Only the compose and mount ones need to become non-constructing. 3. Keep the reconcile guarantee: no reader may see AgentRunsDB before reconcile. Building off-loop and then publishing the bridge satisfies this, because all readers go through the bridge. 4. ensure_activity_receipt_service is already designed for asyncio.to_thread: it closes the worker's connection when get_ident() differs from the owner thread. A cheaper alternative with lower risk is reconcile_on_init=False plus the TASK-32804.10 worker-sweep pattern, together with a lazy data dir in ShadowRepoService. That removes the history-scaling and admission parts even if construction stays on the loop. 5. The launch-wake path (console_launch_wake.py:271) also constructs on the loop and should use the same off-loop build.

title: Every ChaChaNotes/AgentRuns transaction pays the storage-admission handshake (~245 open() calls), and run_owned_db_call reconnects through the helper process on each call
trigger: Every ChaChaNotes and AgentRuns transaction app-wide. Hot instances in this slice: F3 (on the loop, per tick), F4 (per tick), F5 (per keystroke), F7 (on the loop, per tick while drilled in).
cost: Measured independently in cProfile: 20 x _read_database_scope_metadata = 40 transactions, 9,800 posix.open calls (245 per transaction), 0.31 s in _acquire_storage. That is about 5 ms per single-row transaction (get_local_authority_id at 6.1 ms direct) on a deep scratch path; a real profile is probably about half. run_owned_db_call cost 67.7 ms per call versus 12.6 ms on a kept connection, so about 55 ms per call is helper-process connect and teardown.
fix: Amortise admission per thread or per operation scope: cache the verified parent-directory fds or identity and revalidate only on generation or pause changes (the same fix TASK-32804.1 AC#2 asks for, applied in storage_admission rather than only in config). For run_owned_db_call, keep one registered reader connection per executor thread, or use a dedicated DB executor, instead of connecting and closing per call.
fix_notes: High risk. The admission path enforces backup-recovery pause and generation fencing and ADR-029 private-path trust. Any cache of verified directory identity must be invalidated on generation, pause and selector changes, and must still refuse during maintenance. run_owned_db_call retires connections deliberately, so that maintenance quiescence can drain handles and cancelled awaiters do not leak them. A retained per-executor-thread connection must be registered with the quiescence registry and closed on maintenance. A dedicated single DB reader thread with one registered connection is the safer shape. Separately, spawning a helper process per connection open is the dominant constant; skipping the helper prepare when the path identity is unchanged since the last verified open would need a security review.

title: Raw CLI streaming creates a new OS thread (threading.Timer) for every 50 ms repaint window

The replacement must keep a trailing flush: one long-lived per-invocation flusher thread waiting on a Condition or Event with a 0.05 s timeout, or marshal a single loop-side `set_timer` through `_marshal_to_ui`. Keep `cancel_repaint`'s terminal semantics, so no repaint after finalize.

title: Draft spend refresh debounces by destroying and recreating a Textual Timer on every keystroke, then runs the full settings-summary sync
trigger: Yes. Every composer draft mutation while the active session has no run in an active status. refresh fires once per 0.2 s typing pause.

The fix must be 'reset() if the timer is pending, else set_timer()', tracking pending state via the existing `self.timer = None` in refresh. Alternatively, keep a monotonic deadline and let a single timer re-arm itself if the deadline moved. The benefit is marginal, so this is optional hygiene.

title: Workspace-tree page load reads the full, unpaged membership list synchronously on the loop, twice per page
trigger: Expanding a named workspace in the Console rail tree, pressing load-more, or retrying. Two to three full membership reads per page, on the loop.

title: Terminal manager notifications use blocking call_from_thread per parser turn, coupling PTY I/O to UI-loop latency
trigger: Every parser turn of every attached session while the Terminal workspace view is attached. Keystroke delivery and PTY reads stall for the whole time the loop is busy.
cost: Estimated, not measured. It adds one loop round-trip of latency per output turn on the I/O thread. Output throughput for large outputs is capped by loop responsiveness, and keystroke-to-shell delivery waits behind any loop stall.
fix: Use fire-and-forget marshalling: screen.app._loop.call_soon_threadsafe(callback), or post a message. _queue_refresh already coalesces with _frame_pending, and generation guards make a late callback harmless.
fix_notes: Fire-and-forget marshalling needs: (1) a guard for a closed or None loop during shutdown, since call_soon_threadsafe raises RuntimeError; (2) preserving Textual's active-app context, which call_from_thread gets from app._context(). _queue_refresh ends in screen.call_after_refresh, and that needs the right app context. screen.post_message is thread-safe and avoids touching the private _loop, so prefer it or wrap the callback. The generation guards already make a late or dropped callback harmless.
reason: Code matches the finding. _marshal_terminal_to_ui (wiring.py:635-640) calls screen.app.call_from_thread(callback) from off-loop threads. In the installed Textual 8.2.8, App.call_from_thread does run_coroutine_threadsafe(...) and then future.result(), so the calling thread blocks until the loop runs the callback. The calling thread is the per-session runtime thread: _run_runtime (session_manager.py:1328-1373) does take_input and _write_runtime_input, then process_output. process_output calls _notify_subscribers (session_manager.py:598, 1596-1603), which runs ConsoleTerminalController._manager_changed (terminal.py:441-444), then _marshal_to_ui. After that the same thread reads PTY output. The callback only runs _queue_refresh, which is already coalesced by _frame_pending, so the blocking round-trip buys nothing. It chains the terminal's input and output pump to loop latency, which includes F2's 19 ms-per-session snapshots in the resulting _refresh frame. No open task covers it.

title: Session-tab and workspace switches do synchronous registry reads and writes on the loop, bypassing the generation cache
trigger: Every session-tab switch (one read; plus writes when the tabs are in different workspaces), every workspace-tree activation (a write plus a context rebuild), and every Console resume (one read).

title: Appearance-map TTL cache can never hit when a requested id has no live conversations row, so every merge re-queries SQLite
trigger: State: an open native tab whose persisted conversation was soft-deleted, for example via the Console rail's own Delete action on an open row (chat_screen.py:7259, then confirm_console_conversation_delete) or via Library. While in that state, every workspace-context build (5 Hz while streaming) and every Ctrl+K switcher poll (5 Hz) misses the cache.
cost: Estimated only. Each miss is one `SELECT id, metadata FROM conversations WHERE id IN (...) AND deleted = 0` on the event loop, PK-indexed and roughly 0.05-0.3 ms including the quiescence lock. About 20 queries/s gives roughly 1-6 ms/s while streaming, and only in this state. Minor.
fix: Record queried-but-absent ids in the cache as a negative entry (for example ('', '')), so the subset check passes until TTL expiry or an appearance write.
fix_notes: Do not put a ('', '') sentinel into the map. _apply_console_browser_appearance_state (workspace.py:3071) treats any present key as authoritative and would blank icon/color for that id. That is harmless for a deleted id, but it is a semantic change. Safer: keep a separate absent-id set stamped with the same cache_at/TTL, test `wanted <= set(cached_map) | absent`, and clear it wherever the map cache is cleared (the appearance-write invalidation). Alternatively, fix the root state by unbinding or closing the native session on soft-delete, but that is a behaviour change outside a perf fix.

    and now - cache_at < CONSOLE_APPEARANCE_MAP_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS
    and wanted <= set(cached_map)):

The failed call re-queries and resets cache_at. Native rows (workspace.py:3162) carry session.persisted_conversation_id regardless of DB state. The trigger state is reachable from inside Console, not only from Library: _delete_console_conversation (workspace.py:7764) soft-deletes and only refreshes the browser, without closing or unbinding the open session. I counted merges per build: 2 in _current_console_browser_rows (4121, 4132) and 2 in _with_console_conversation_browser_state (4298, 4372). All four carry the native row, so a stuck state costs about 4 batched PK queries per build, or about 20/s at 5 Hz while streaming. console_session_switcher_active_entries (3355) calls the map directly and is polled at 200 ms by the switcher modal. The finder's wording that it calls _merge_console_browser_rows is slightly off, but the effect is the same: its 'memory-only' docstring is violated every tick in this state, and every 2 s even when healthy. TASK-31506 covers the switcher's projection recompute, not this cache miss.

All of it runs synchronously on the event loop.

A run-group click is about 2x that plus load_grid. preflight_for_bench (bench click): 27 / 110 / 542 ms. Rail reads per compose: 48 / 149 / 577 ms.

title: Library source snapshot deep-copied on the loop 2-3 times per visit and after every mutation
corrected: tldw_chatbook/UI/Library_Modules/library_snapshot_cache.py:82; tldw_chatbook/UI/Screens/library_screen.py:11438 (the per-refresh hot site); tldw_chatbook/UI/Screens/library_screen.py:12969 (the seed, first construction only, since the route is reusable)
trigger: There is one clone per snapshot refresh, on the loop. It fires on each Library visit (on_screen_resume, then `_refresh_library_visit_surfaces`, then library_screen.py:9403) and after each Prompts, Skills, Notes or ingest mutation that calls `_refresh_local_source_snapshot`. The seed clones at `__init__` and `restore_state` run only on first construction of the reusable screen, and only while the app cache is under 5 s old. Warm revisits never reach them.

Deepcopy took 0.91 ms median and 0.96 ms max. The two validation passes add very little. Expect about 1 ms per visit or mutation on warm paths, not 3-7 ms. Strings are shared by deepcopy, so large note bodies do not raise the cost. The cost scales with the number of records and keys, and page caps bound both.

fix_notes: `_apply_local_source_snapshot` (library_screen.py:12865-12873) already copies the top-level dicts. It keeps references to the inner record Mappings in `_local_source_records`, so the clone is there to stop later in-place record mutation from leaking into the app cache. Freezing or sharing without a copy needs an audit of every writer of those record dicts first. The lowest-risk wins are: (1) drop the second `_is_valid_library_source_snapshot` pass, since deepcopy of a validated tuple keeps its structure; (2) make the seed read-side clone shallow, because it runs once per app run anyway. Given the roughly 1 ms size, this is hygiene only and not worth a medium-risk freeze refactor.

reason:
The code is on the pin. library_snapshot_cache.py:82 does copy.deepcopy between two _is_valid_library_source_snapshot passes. It is called from library_screen.py:11438, inside the `@work(exclusive=True, group="library_source_snapshot")` async `_refresh_local_source_snapshot`. That worker is not threaded, so the clone runs on the event loop. The other caller is library_screen.py:12969 in `_seed_local_source_snapshot_from_cache`.

The 'two to three times per visit' claim is wrong. The Library route is `reusable=True` (screen_registry.py:114, TASK-31521). app.py:13468-13523 reuses the installed instance on warm visits and skips both construction and `restore_state`. So the seed clones from `__init__` (library_screen.py:4143) and `restore_state` (library_screen.py:10398) fire only when an instance is first constructed. Even then they fire only if the app cache is under 5 s old (LIBRARY_SNAPSHOT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS=5.0).

The real steady state is one clone per `_refresh_local_source_snapshot`. That runs once per visit, from the resume path at library_screen.py:9403, and once per Prompts, Skills, Notes or ingest mutation (roughly 25 call sites across the controllers). It only clones when lookup_error is None. The snapshot is bounded: 100 notes, 50 media and 20 conversations (LIBRARY_SOURCE_PAGE_SIZES, and LIBRARY_CONVERSATION_PAGE_SIZE=20), plus the prompts count and a skills payload. So this is a minor loop cost of about 1 ms, which fits P3.

Holding one lease across a derivation does NOT help by itself, because the hold was not the cost. Any fastpath keyed on file identity must keep the recovery and selection-change checks (binding(), selection_changed) that the guarded path enforces, since these are security-relevant policy files. Both are awaited on the loop with no to_thread; _sync_children has 51 call sites and _sync_permissions_mode has 28. Inside the fence, capture runs `_tool_policy_inventory` (read_profile_inventory_snapshot/read_snapshot_strict, a file read plus json plus sha256). It then runs `_resolve_effective_states` -> `UnifiedMCPControlPlaneService.effective_tool_states` (unified_control_plane_service.py:5219), which does `store.load()` and possibly `mark_config_changed` (a write). A second inventory read follows, and a third on drift. Other threads do contend for the lock. BuiltinToolGate._load_payload (builtin_tool_gate.py:308) does `store.load()` on agent worker threads once per turn, the MCP gate reads at unified_control_plane_service.py:5456/5546/5597 do the same, and the Console's offloaded setters take the fence too. The finding overstates the extra cost the outer fence adds. `load()` (:773) and every setter already take the same lock, so the loop could already block on a worker's write inside `effective_tool_states` without this fence. The fence only widens the loop-side hold window from the single load() to the whole 2-3-read capture. Contention needs a worker-thread write (a Console always-allow approval or a rug-pull mark) that overlaps an MCP-hub sync pass. That coincidence is rare, the worker side waits on a background thread (harmless), and the loop-side wait is bounded by one small JSON atomic write (~13 ms per the task-32804.7 measurement). The workbench's own `_call_profile_scoped_off_loop` writes are awaited before the resync, so the widget cannot contend with itself. The ~39 ms hold is the on-loop capture cost itself, which is F1/F3's loop-blocking finding and not new cost from this finding. P3 is right: this is a real but narrow widening of an existing lock contention, with no independent hot trigger. No open task covers it. TASK-32804.7 (Done) offloaded the permission-store writes and config reads but left capture() on the loop.

Every start_* site must resume the poll: backup, inspect, restore, extraction, rollback, delete-copy and recovered-media actions. So must an operation that is already running at on_mount (started earlier or by another surface). Missing one resume leaves the status stale. A lower-risk alternative is to keep the interval and add a timer-path-only guard, `if current is self._last_snapshot: return`. title: Chunking Lab sample editor publishes an undebounced whole-sample session edit per keystroke (O(sample) joins on the loop, hash/model_dump/prune in a thread, full refresh with ~25 query_one)

title: Render plans for immutable revisions are recompiled on every frame load; import then plan compiles the same source twice
trigger: Every canvas frame load: open, navigate or select, and each follow reload after a new revision. Open-in-Canvas always compiles twice.

ADR-121 ('Interactive compilation ownership') says 'No extra executor, source cache, database owner, or revision writer is introduced' and 'A completed prepared plan remains operation-local'. compilation.py's module docstring repeats 'without owning ... source caches'. A plan LRU therefore needs an ADR amendment first. ADR-124 requires cache identity to include compiler/security policy as well as exact source and profile manifest, so key on (content_sha256, runtime_profile, snapshot build/manifest id, compiler policy version), not just sha and profile. Plans are derived from source, so a bounded LRU retains source-derived data in memory. The fix_risk is medium, not low.

title: Canvas package __init__ eagerly imports models onto the boot path; no production code imports from the package root
trigger: Boot, via the config import.
cost: Measured with -X importtime on 'import tldw_chatbook.config': Canvas.models self time is 5.3, 10.2 and 11.4 ms across runs. However, on the default landing tab (Console), console_canvas_controller imports Canvas.models before first paint anyway (see F5). The fix therefore only moves the cost for Console-landing users. It yields a real saving only when the landing screen is not Console, or together with the F5 lazy fix. That is minor, hence P3.
fix: Make Canvas/__init__.py a PEP 562 lazy facade (the Local_Ingestion template: __getattr__ mapping names to submodules), or drop the re-exports. config.py keeps importing Canvas.limits directly.
fix_notes: A PEP 562 __getattr__ facade (the Local_Ingestion template) or dropping the re-exports is safe, since nothing imports those symbols from the package root. Pair it with F5 for any first-paint benefit.
evidence:
from .limits import CanvasLimitError, CanvasLimits
from .models import (CanvasBridgeRequest, ..., RuntimeProfile,)   # Canvas/__init__.py
from tldw_chatbook.Canvas.limits import CanvasLimits              # config.py module scope
reason: Canvas/__init__.py:3-14 eagerly imports limits and models. config.py:68 imports Canvas.limits at module scope, so models loads at boot. Canvas.archive, which is also preloaded, imports only limits, not models. So models on the boot path comes solely from __init__. A grep of tldw_chatbook and Tests finds no symbol import from the package root: all 17 'from tldw_chatbook.Canvas import X' hits import submodules (guide, profiles, runtime_assets, service, native_authority, control_protocol, authoring).

title: Canvas policy watcher polls config at 4 Hz via asyncio.to_thread for the whole process lifetime, even with no gateway or authority
corrected: tldw_chatbook/Chat/console_runtime.py:2924 is inside start_async_lifecycles (def at 2915); the watcher loop body is 3031-3047
trigger: Always on from app mount for the whole process lifetime, with or without Canvas use.
cost: Measured the same pattern with the real get_canvas_execution_enabled in an isolated env. A single read is 2.2 us. Over 8 s idle, a baseline loop used 0.2 ms CPU and the watcher loop used 10.3 ms CPU, so about 0.13% of a core, plus about 8 loop wakeups/s and 4 executor wakeups/s. That is about 8x below the P0 1%-idle bar, so it is a minor always-on wakeup cost: P3, not P2.
fix: Keep the 0.25 s cadence only while _canvas_gateway or _canvas_native_authority exists, and back off to about 5 s (or event-driven on the config-generation publish or settings save) otherwise. The latch semantics are unchanged. Update the pinning test's timing, not its contract.
fix_notes: The pinning test waits at most 1.0 s for the watcher to latch a disable on Home with no gateway. A 5 s idle backoff breaks that timeout, so the test's timing must change. That is safe because every canvas_enabled() read already latches a false observation itself. An event-driven trigger on config save or generation publish is cleaner than a backoff. The served parent loop should get the same treatment.
evidence:
while not self._canvas_maintenance_closed:
    reader = asyncio.create_task(asyncio.to_thread(self._canvas_enabled), ...)
    enabled = await asyncio.shield(reader)
    ...
    await asyncio.sleep(0.25)
reason: _watch_canvas_policy (console_runtime.py:3031-3047) loops every 0.25 s, doing create_task(asyncio.to_thread(self._canvas_enabled)) then asyncio.sleep(0.25), until disabled. start_async_lifecycles:2915 runs it from app mount (app.py:14739), and Tests/UI/test_console_runtime_ownership.py (around 2380) pins that it runs on Home with no controller or gateway. It stops only on disable or maintenance close. The served parent has its own 0.25 s loop (serve.py:913-918), which reads config on the loop directly without to_thread.

title: Settings > Privacy Canvas card resolves the served-auth policy on the loop: getaddrinfo each time, keyring for remote configs (gap in Done TASK-33081)
known_task: TASK-33081 (Done; gap: the Settings Privacy path was not converted)
trigger: Opening Settings > Privacy & Security, or any detail-pane recompose, composes the Canvas card: 3 builds. Each Canvas checkbox toggle does 1 build. Save and revert do 2 more. All run synchronously on the Textual loop.
cost: Default local config: getaddrinfo('localhost') measured on this Mac at 0.27 ms warm and 5.9 ms cold. That is about 9 calls, roughly 2.5 ms per Privacy render, which is minor. Remote-served config with the token in the OS keyring (the recommended setup per config.py:5916-5919): 3 synchronous keyring lookups per render and 1 per toggle. On Linux SecretService/D-Bus that is plausibly 10-100+ ms each (the TASK-33081 Fedora incident class), so a 30-300 ms freeze on a settings visit. P2: it is a settings path and depends on the config.
fix: For _canvas_draft_value/_stage_canvas_value, read only config._normalize_canvas_execution plus auto_open (no remote-access resolution). Compute the full CanvasConfigPolicy once with asyncio.to_thread when the Privacy pane opens, and cache it on the screen for remote_access_summary.
fix_notes: compose() cannot await. Yield the remote-access summary row with a placeholder and fill it from a thread worker (run_worker(thread=True) or to_thread in on_mount) that builds the full policy once and caches it on the screen. For _canvas_draft_value and _stage_canvas_value, read only enabled/auto_open, via a keyring-free, resolver-free path such as a flag on build_canvas_config_policy that skips _canvas_remote_access_status. Do NOT pass a keyring_get stub to the summary build, or the summary would wrongly show 'refused'. _reconcile_canvas_runtime_policy (settings_screen.py:30331, 30387) on the save path also builds the full policy and should get the same skip-remote treatment.
evidence:
def _loaded_canvas_policy(self):

title: Integrity-pinned runtime JS (738 KB quickjs + about 200 KB worker/renderer) is served no-store, so it is re-fetched and re-instantiated on every canvas frame load
trigger: canvas_shell.js loadFrame sets ui.frame.src = renderer_url (line 695) on boot, navigate/select and follow-reload after 'updated' events (pollEvents, lines 790-812). Each renderer load constructs a new Worker, which imports quickjs-runtime.js.
cost: About 0.9 MB of loopback body per frame load, written from the Textual loop in native mode: roughly 1-3 ms of loop time (estimated). Browser-side re-parse and instantiation is real but lives outside the TUI process, and per (3) it is likely unavoidable in Chromium.
fix: For the session-free runtime assets only (the canvas_renderer*/canvas_runtime_worker*/quickjs-runtime.js inventory), serve under a content-hash path segment with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable. Keep no-store for everything session-bound.
fix_notes: no-store is pinned by tests (Tests/Canvas/test_gateway.py:1133/1226/1592; Tests/Canvas/browser/test_canvas_zero_egress.py:237/254/1751) and is part of the zero-egress security posture, so a change needs an ADR-121/124-level decision. Static URLs already embed shell_incarnation_id (gateway.py:1582), so any cache reuse is per shell incarnation only. Verify in Chromium that a sandboxed/opaque-origin frame and a data:-URL worker actually hit the cache before investing. Otherwise the gain is Firefox/Safari only.
reason: Code verified. _security_headers_middleware (gateway.py:1615) sets Cache-Control: no-store on every response, including /static/. _static_asset (2372-2389) serves the runtime inventory (quickjs-runtime.js is 737,944 bytes; worker and renderer are 53-85 KB each). The served-mode public_runtime_asset sets no-store explicitly (gateway.py:2405). The renderer builds the worker from a data: URL bootstrap that dynamically imports canvas_runtime_worker*.js (canvas_renderer.js:1265-1268), which imports quickjs-runtime.js. So each frame load re-transfers about 0.9 MB. Downgraded to P3 for three reasons. (1) The TUI-loop cost is only aiohttp writing about 1 MB over loopback, roughly 1-3 ms per frame load. The heavy part, JS parse and WASM instantiate, happens in the browser, not on the scarce Textual loop. (2) Frame loads come from boot, navigation and follow reloads after agent revisions, not a per-key or per-tick path. (3) The proposed fix probably does nothing in Chromium. The renderer runs in an opaque-origin sandbox (CSP 'sandbox allow-scripts' at gateway.py:123, iframe sandbox='allow-scripts'), and the worker is a data: URL. Under Chrome's split HTTP cache, requests from opaque-origin frames get a transient network isolation key and are not cached whatever the headers say. Firefox and Safari, which partition by top-level site, would benefit. No open task covers it.

title: ConsoleCanvasController holds a threading.RLock across SQLite service calls that UI-loop paths also take
trigger: A worker-thread canvas update_canvas/create_canvas holds the lock during DB reads while the loop enters list_session_canvases/read_session_canvas (gateway handlers) or capture_selected_scope (the start of another session's agent reply).
cost: Estimated. The loop waits up to the worker's remaining lock-hold time: about 3 point or ancestor-path reads plus a sha256 of up to 512 KiB in validate(), so a few ms to tens of ms at large path lengths. It happens only under concurrency.
fix: Take the lock only to snapshot or mutate stage state, and do the _service_call I/O outside it, revalidating the generation after. Once F4 moves UI-side calls off the loop, the loop no longer waits on this lock.
fix_notes: Moving the _service_call I/O outside the lock is risky. The lock currently makes the stale-parent check and the sequence allocation atomic against concurrent updates to the same canvas and against run commit/discard, so revalidation after reacquiring needs careful generation fencing. The safer, smaller fix is to move the loop-side callers off the loop instead (asyncio.to_thread around capture_selected_scope in _run_agent_reply, and around the sync authority calls in the native gateway handlers). The loop then never contends on this lock.
evidence:
with self._lock:
    ...
    read = self._service_call("read_canvas", scope, canvas_id)       # DB under lock
    ...
    sequence=self._next_sequence(stage, canvas_id, parent),          # 2 more DB calls under lock
# list_session_canvases / read_session_canvas: with self._lock: self._service_call(...)
reason: Verified: ConsoleCanvasController._lock is a threading.RLock (console_canvas_controller.py:374). _update_canvas holds it across _service_call('read_canvas') at 1153 and _next_sequence, which does next_revision_sequence (1854) and list_canvases (1861), all under the same 'with self._lock' at 1109. read_canvas at 572-582 also does DB I/O under the lock, and update_canvas takes that path between the preflight and the final acquisition. _service_call (1711-1727) runs the durable service method synchronously. Loop-side waiters exist. console_chat_controller.py:28369 is inside async _run_agent_reply (not threaded), and it calls capture_selected_scope, which takes the controller lock and then, through native_authority._capture_selected_scope, calls _read_exact -> read_session_canvas (lock plus DB, 1011-1013). Native gateway handlers call the sync authority through _maybe_await on the loop (list_session_canvases 988/994, read_session_canvas 1011), for example /api/state and /api/plan after a follow event. Canvas tool calls run on the agent worker thread. So the loop can block on the RLock while another session's worker holds it across up to about 3 DB calls. This requires concurrency (a fleet or a parallel session's canvas tool, or browser access during a tool call), so P3 stands.

title: Browser shell polls /api/events every 350 ms per open canvas tab for as long as the tab stays open
trigger: While any Canvas browser tab is open: about 2.9 req/s per tab, forever. Background-tab timer throttling lowers the rate but does not stop it.
cost: Estimated at about 0.3-0.5 ms of aiohttp handling per poll, about 1-1.5 ms/s of loop time per open tab (about 0.1-0.15% core), plus loop wakeups. That is below the P0 idle-tax threshold of ~1% core, so P3.
fix: Long-poll: hold /api/events on an asyncio.Event per (session, canvas) that _publish sets, with about a 25 s timeout. The client loop stays the same apart from dropping the 350 ms delay.
fix_notes: Long-poll needs matching changes in the served-mode parent-to-child control protocol, cancellation on close, revoke and dispose, and re-running the selection_epoch and _session_is_current checks after the wait. A lower-risk first step: stop or slow polling while document.hidden, and back off exponentially (350 ms up to about 5 s) when polls return no events, resetting after user actions.
reason: Verified at canvas_shell.js:821: 'if (!closed) pollTimer = window.setTimeout(pollEvents, 350)'. It re-arms unconditionally in finally. grep finds no visibilitychange or document.hidden gating in canvas_shell.js. Each poll hits gateway._events (gateway.py:1993): _require_session plus authority.read_events plus json_response. read_events (native_authority.py:964) is a sync dict/tuple copy. The native gateway's aiohttp site is started on the Textual loop (chat_screen.py:21386 -> open_canvas_with_textual), so polls are handled on the UI loop. No open task covers canvas event polling.

title: NativeConsoleCanvasAuthority._events grows for the process lifetime and is fully copied on each poll
trigger: Every canvas publication appends an event that is never evicted. Every 350 ms browser poll copies the per-key list.
cost: Estimated at about 0.5-1 KB per event. Even hundreds of revisions stay in the hundreds of KB, and the per-poll tuple copy and scan costs microseconds. Hygiene only.
fix: Use collections.deque(maxlen=64) per key. The client already treats an unknown cursor as 'last event only' (read_events returns events[-1:]).
fix_notes: deque(maxlen=64) is compatible with the existing uses: setdefault(...).append, the prior_events[-1] check and pop() in gateway_scope, and tuple() in read_events. All three setdefault(..., []) sites must change to deque. When a cursor is evicted, read_events returns events[-1:], which the shell already handles as follow-latest. Optionally also drop keys for disposed or deleted conversations. Low risk.
reason: Verified: NativeConsoleCanvasAuthority._events (native_authority.py:203) is appended to at 395 (via _publish per revision), 642, 946 and 1255 (_publish). The only trimming is gateway_scope popping one trailing 'disconnected' event (703-707) and dispose() clearing everything (274). read_events (964-973) tuple-copies the whole per-key list and scans it linearly for the cursor on every poll. Growth is proportional to canvas publications (revisions, imports, selection changes), not to time, and each event is small, so this is not a meaningful long-session leak.

title: Turn-commit canvas batch validation walks the ancestor chain with one SELECT per message inside the write transaction
trigger: Once per assistant turn (or temporary-session promotion) that commits canvas revisions, inside the Console persistence write transaction.
cost: Measured with an in-memory SQLite micro-benchmark (PK lookups, 50k noise rows): 1.9 ms for a 1000-message path and 6.4 ms for 4096. That excludes the per-statement quiescence tax (TASK-31502), which adds to each of the N statements. It extends write-lock hold on a rare path, so P3.
fix: Use one recursive CTE (WITH RECURSIVE path(id, parent, conv, deleted, depth) ... LIMIT 4097) and validate in Python, as _require_durable_active_path already does with a single IN query.
fix_notes: A WITH RECURSIVE walk keyed on messages.id with a depth column and LIMIT 4097 must keep three checks: cycle detection (a recursive CTE with UNION ALL loops on a cycle until the LIMIT, so detect a repeated id or depth > cap in Python), the conversation_id match, and the deleted=0 check on every row. Ideally also rejecting at the first bad row, as the loop does. Capture a query plan per the repo's index-plan rule if any index assumptions change.
reason: Verified at repository.py:921-935. _validate_append_batch walks parent_message_id with one 'SELECT parent_message_id, conversation_id, deleted FROM messages WHERE id = ?' per ancestor, capped at MAX_CANVAS_DURABLE_ACTIVE_PATH_MESSAGES = 4096 (limits.py:26). It runs inside the write transaction through append_batch_in_transaction (832/856) <- console_transaction_contribution.py:178 <- console_canvas_controller.py:198 (turn contribution write). Only turns that staged canvas revisions reach it. The same module already validates a path with a single IN query (_require_durable_active_path, 1303-1348), and a recursive-CTE precedent exists (console_dispatch_repository.py:92).

title: Ingest registry listener does O(queue) work per notification and remounts the whole queue panel per job transition, making folder submit O(N^2) and every tick a full queue remount
trigger: Yes. Clicking Start on the Import canvas runs the synchronous per-file submit loop, which fires the listener N times on the UI thread with the Import canvas selected. Each later mark_parsing, mark_writing, mark_done and mark_failed arrives through call_from_thread and fires it again. Up to 500 persisted jobs are restored across restarts (app.py:2403), so the queue the listener walks and renders includes history.
cost: Measured in isolation with the real registry and build_library_ingest_state. jobs() costs 0.75 / 2.28 / 4.15 ms and the state build 1.02 / 2.92 / 5.22 ms at 100 / 300 / 500 jobs. A submit loop whose listener does the state build, a second copy and the counts takes 130 ms at 100 files and 1,211 ms at 300 files, which is quadratic before any DOM work. A generic Textual recompose of the same row shape (Static, progress Static, Horizontal and Button per row) measured 217-267 ms at 100 rows and 713-975 ms at 300 rows. That cost is paid on every job transition while the Import canvas is open.
fix: (1) Coalesce: the listener only marks the canvas dirty and schedules one call_after_refresh (or a set_timer of about 50 ms) that runs _update_library_ingest_dynamic_regions once, so a folder submit pays one rebuild. (2) Use the non-copying registry.iter_jobs_for_listeners() (added by TASK-32804.5) in _build_library_ingest_state and _library_landing_attention_action, and skip the attention computation unless the landing is visible and not suspended. (3) Key LibraryIngestQueuePanel rows by job_id: Static.update the rows that changed and mount or remove only the delta instead of refresh(recompose=True). Alternatively, render active rows plus the newest ~50 with a 'Show N older' control. That also bounds the Import-canvas compose. New evidence versus TASK-32804.5: its AC#1 was checked against the app listener only, and the Library screen listener keeps the submit quadratic.
fix_notes: (1) Coalesce only the dynamic-region rebuild and the attention recompute, with one call_after_refresh per dirty burst. Keep the per-notification batch-settle baseline and active-count crossing logic synchronous: it depends on seeing each crossing, and the counts are O(N) but cheap. Note that refresh(recompose=True) already coalesces within a loop turn; the quadratic cost is the state build and the copies. (2) iter_jobs_for_listeners yields live registry objects. It is safe for the attention computation, but build_library_ingest_state must not keep live job references in LibraryIngestCanvasState, or the old_state/new_state structural comparison can alias. Materialise the rows from it rather than storing jobs. (3) Keyed row diffing has to respect the task-32231 group collapse, the in-place progress patching by #library-ingest-progress-{job_id}, and focus restore (TASK-31583). Bounding the rendered history ('Show N older') is the lower-risk first step.
evidence:
library_screen.py:20507  new_state = self._build_library_ingest_state()   # jobs_fn() deep-copies every job (20614)
library_screen.py:20529  summary.refresh(recompose=True)
library_screen.py:20530  queue.refresh(recompose=True)            # remounts every row (Static + Horizontal + 1-4 Buttons)
library_screen.py:14113  live = tuple(job for job in jobs_fn() if ...)   # _library_landing_attention_action, 2nd full copy
library_ingest_controller.py:1308  attention = self._library_landing_attention_action()   # unconditional, even while suspended
library_ingest_jobs.py:853-856  self._jobs.append(job); self._notify_listeners()   # once per submitted file
reason: Checked the code at the audit pin. The registry listener is added in on_mount (library_screen.py:9517). It delegates to LibraryIngestController._handle_library_ingest_registry_changed (library_ingest_controller.py:1135). On the Import canvas, when not suspended, it calls _update_library_ingest_dynamic_regions (library_screen.py:20461). That rebuilds the state through _build_library_ingest_state, whose jobs() at 20614 deep-copies every job with _copy_job, then calls summary.refresh(recompose=True) and queue.refresh(recompose=True) (20529-20530). On every notification, suspended or not, it also runs _library_landing_attention_action (controller:1308 -> library_screen.py:14113), which is a second full jobs() copy. registry.submit calls _notify_listeners once per file (library_ingest_jobs.py:852-856), and app.submit_library_ingest_job loops over expanded folder files synchronously (app.py:3233). Only the app's own listener uses iter_jobs_for_listeners (app.py:2672); the Library screen never does. So TASK-32804.5's AC#1 fix does not cover this listener. The queue panel (library_ingest_canvas.py:556) composes one row per job, and DONE rows are not collapsed, because _GROUPABLE_ROW_STATES is FAILED/SKIPPED/CANCELLED only. Worker-thread transitions reach the listener through call_from_thread as separate loop turns, so each one recomposes the whole panel.

title: Most Library destination switches and cross-route opens still do a whole-screen await self.recompose() (nav, footer, rail and canvas remounted)
trigger: Yes. Rail-row and hub-action presses, in-canvas row switches (the i/n accelerators, export back-origin, etc.) and item opens across reader shells all run in async message handlers on the loop. This is the core Library navigation gesture.
cost: Not re-measured, because mounting the Library screen needs the app. The repo's own Phase C design record (Docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-01-library-screen-decomposition-design.md, around line 352) measured this mechanism, a whole-screen recompose on a rail switch, at 124 ms median block, 187 ms CPU and 114-179 mounts, against 29 ms with residency. This fits the P0 bar of ≳100 ms on a common path. The TASK-23025 figure of 640-790 ms was measured under an instrumented harness and is an upper bound, not a typical cost.
fix: Generalize Phase C: when the reader shell changes, rebuild only the `#library-shell-grid` subtree. Compose the destination route's shell into the grid with remove_children + mount and keep the header, nav bar, footer and ideally the rail widget, patching the rail with rail.apply_selection. Alternatively, extend library_browse_route_for_canvas_kind residency to the Conversations, Prompts, Skills and Collections shells. Replace the `bool(self.query(selector))` probes with the existing _library_layout_ref cache or query_one+NoMatches. Related open umbrella: TASK-281, which covered only the selection interactions.
fix_notes: The design record lists hazards that any extension must honour. Widget.recompose() destroys residency. DOM presence is used elsewhere as a route proxy, and residency silently breaks it (focus can land in a hidden resident canvas). A resident but unselected canvas keeps processing row events. Mixed display booleans must become class toggles. Extending residency route by route (Conversations, Prompts, Skills, Collections shells) is safer than a generic 'rebuild only #library-shell-grid', because the header, rail and footer registration still have to be re-applied, as swap_library_browse_route does. Replacing the bool(self.query()) probes with _library_layout_ref or query_one is low risk and independent of the rest.

    ... _replace_library_canvas_child(...)
elif await self._replace_library_browse_canvas(shell):   # only Media<->Notes inside the resident shell
    replaced = True
if not replaced:
    await self.recompose()                                # 22470

reason: Read the code of _select_library_rail_row_after_source_admission (library_screen.py:22451-22470). A targeted update happens only in two cases. The first is when the destination is an ordinary route: _library_ordinary_route_active (5602) excludes Media, Conversations, Notes, Prompts, Skills, the three Create rows and artifacts-*, and #library-canvas-route-content must be mounted. The second is swap_library_browse_route, which returns False unless #library-browse-reader-shell is already mounted and the destination kind is media or database notes (library_browse_route_swap.py:98+). Every other switch runs await self.recompose() at 22470: landing -> Media or Notes, any switch into or out of Conversations, Prompts, Skills, Create or Artifacts, and Media/Notes -> an ordinary route. Rail presses reach this through handle_library_rail_row (22120-22161), the Button.Pressed handler on .library-rail-row and .library-hub-action. _apply_library_open_item_surface (12383-12405) does 7 bool(self.query()) full-DOM probes, then a whole-screen recompose whenever the reader shell differs. TASK-281 (In Progress, all ACs checked) inventoried rail-changing navigation as 'full recompose stays', and Phase C covered only Media<->Notes. The remaining routes are therefore new scope with no open task.

title: Each keystroke in the Library Search/RAG query box rebuilds the provider gate, which calls config.load_settings() (6-7.5 ms warm), plus 3-6 full-DOM query walks
corrected: tldw_chatbook/config.py:1862 (the @guarded decorator on load_settings itself is why a warm hit pays the handshake); tldw_chatbook/Backup_Recovery/config_participants.py:376 (guarded definition)
known_task: TASK-32804.1 (related root cause; its fix did not cover load_settings)
trigger: Yes. The handler fires once per typed character on the Search/RAG canvas and is awaited on the screen's message pump. The same state build also runs on evidence select/open/stage, scope/mode toggles and outcome application.
cost: Measured in isolation (scratch HOME, XDG and TLDW_CONFIG_PATH): warm config.load_settings() median 15.9 ms, p95 20.8 ms; library_rag_answer_provider_gate() median 15.7 ms, p95 18.4 ms; warm get_cli_setting 0.0014 ms for comparison. The host was loaded by parallel agents, so absolute numbers may run about 2x the finder's 6-7.5 ms. Either way it is ≥6 ms per keystroke before the DOM walks and callout remounts.
fix: (1) In the query-only refresh, do not rebuild the provider gate: typed text cannot change provider readiness. Build the query/run-gate state from a screen-level gate memo keyed on (current_config_identity(), subscription_readiness_revision()), and pass background_credentials=True for UI checks. (2) Root cause, shared with every load_settings caller: give config.load_settings() the same warm-hit fast path TASK-32804.1 gave get_cli_setting, serving _SETTINGS_CACHE before the admission wrapper (in scope of the TASK-32804.1 family). (3) Replace `not self.query('#library-search-rag-panel')` with query_one+NoMatches.
fix_notes: Memoising the gate on (current_config_identity(), subscription readiness revision) is correct only if every config write bumps that identity. Verify that settings saves and api-key edits invalidate it, or the run gate goes stale after a key is added. The root-cause fix, serving _SETTINGS_CACHE before the guarded handshake the way TASK-32804.1 did for get_cli_setting, helps every load_settings caller. It must keep the rebuild path guarded and must still honour _get_effective_config_path changes. Swapping query() truthiness for query_one plus NoMatches is trivially safe.
evidence:
library_screen.py:34386  @on(Input.Changed, "#library-rag-query-input") -> controller.update_library_rag_query
  -> await self._refresh_search_rag_panel_state_widgets(include_results_and_history=False)
library_screen.py:35300/35313  self.query("#library-search-rag-panel")   # full-DOM truthiness walks, twice
library_screen.py:35317  panel_state = self._library_rag_panel_state()
library_screen.py:14524  provider_gate = library_rag_answer_provider_gate()
library_rag_answer_service.py:250  readiness = get_provider_readiness(provider, app_config.load_settings())
reason: The chain holds as quoted. @on(Input.Changed, '#library-rag-query-input') (library_screen.py:34386) goes to the async controller.update_library_rag_query (library_rag_search_controller.py:835). Once the value changes, it awaits _refresh_search_rag_panel_state_widgets(include_results_and_history=False) (35270). That function runs two bool(self.query('#library-search-rag-panel')) walks, then _library_rag_panel_state() (14473). That calls library_rag_answer_provider_gate() at 14524 on every call, and the gate calls get_provider_readiness(provider, app_config.load_settings()) (library_rag_answer_service.py:250) whenever a provider resolves. The default config resolves 'openai'. The root cause is that config.load_settings itself is decorated @_config_participants.guarded (config.py:1862), so even a warm cache hit pays the storage-admission operation() handshake. TASK-32804.1 added a warm fast path only to load_cli_config_and_ensure_existence (get_cli_setting). No open task covers the warm load_settings cost or this keystroke path; task-284 (Done) only removed the results/history rebuild.

title: refresh() override rebuilds the full footer shortcut model on every plain screen refresh and on focus changes, including uncached focus_chain walks and full-DOM row queries
trigger: Partly. The triggers are resize frames (rare for a full-screen user), screen switches (once per visit) and focus changes inside the media viewer. It is not every focus change app-wide.
cost: Estimated only; nothing was measured. focus_chain is O(widgets) and uncached in Textual 8.2.8, which puts it on the order of 0.2-0.7 ms at 100-400 widgets. The whole footer build is plausibly around 1 ms.
fix: In the refresh() override, call _apply_library_notes_footer_context() only when recompose is true; plain repaints cannot change the shortcut set. Elsewhere, memoize the computed shortcut tuple on a cheap signature (selected row, relevant view flags, focused widget id, width bucket, lifecycle, compose generation) and skip the rebuild when it is unchanged. Cache _library_slash_would_land per (focused, compose_generation) instead of rebuilding focus_chain. Read media neighbours from browse-controller state instead of querying `.library-media-row`.
fix_notes: The proposed fix (1), calling it only when recompose is true, is UNSAFE. canvas_sync.py:994-1004 records that the footer tiers flipped by targeted syncs (Notes select mode, sort strip, media type strip) stay honest only because LibraryScreen.refresh re-derives the footer context on every plain refresh; a footer re-derivation in the sync path was removed on that basis. Resize-driven compact transitions also change hide_ancillary. Memoising on a signature is the only safe variant, and the signature must include compact state, focused widget, select/sort flags and emergency stage. Caching _library_slash_would_land per (focused, compose generation) is reasonable.
evidence:
library_screen.py:8507-8516  if recompose: ...capture...
        self._apply_library_notes_footer_context()     # NOT gated on recompose
library_notes_controller.py:2891  # TASK-23025: this method runs on EVERY screen refresh ... several times per resize frame and focus change
library_screen.py:7258  return control is not None and control in self.focus_chain   # via _library_slash_would_land, 1-2x per footer build
library_screen.py:10777  self._register_footer_shortcuts()   # every focus change in the media viewer
library_screen.py:8738  for bar in self.query(LibraryEmergencyReturn):   # full-DOM walk per registration
reason: The code exists as quoted. LibraryScreen.refresh (library_screen.py:8476-8520) calls _apply_library_notes_footer_context() without a recompose gate (8516), and that method rebuilds the shortcut tuple (library_notes_controller.py:2880). The non-Notes branch goes through _library_footer_shortcuts_for_current_state, and _library_focusable uses the uncached Screen.focus_chain (7258). _register_footer_shortcuts (8724) walks self.query(LibraryEmergencyReturn), and on_descendant_focus calls it in the media viewer (~10777). Frequency is lower than claimed, though. In Textual 8.2.8, Screen.refresh() with no arguments is called only on Screen resize (screen.py:1483), mode switch or screen replace (app.py:2654, 2862), the end of delay_update and App.refresh(). Widget focus and blur refresh the widget, not the screen, and Library code has a single plain self.refresh(layout=True) call (6488). TASK-23025 (Done) already cut the per-resize query volume to 10.6 per frame. The remaining cost is about 1 ms (estimated) per resize frame or viewer focus change, well under the P1 threshold, so P3.

title: Module-scope import of Widgets.Console.prompt_variables_dialog drags in the eager Widgets/Console package (+308 modules, ~380 ms) for one action
trigger: Yes for the non-default boot: the Library screen module is imported on the first-paint path when Library is the initial tab. The screen registry is otherwise lazy.
cost: Re-measured A/B in isolation, after importing Navigation.base_app_screen, two runs per arm. With the real package: 641-642 ms, 866 new modules, 46 Console submodules, console_chat_controller loaded. With a stub Widgets.Console package that has a __path__ but no __init__ body: 329-344 ms, 558 modules, 1 Console submodule, controller not loaded. That is about 300 ms and 308 modules, matching the finder.
fix: Move the import into _stage_library_prompt_for_console as a function-local import, which is the file's own documented lazy-import pattern (e.g. the library_browse_route_swap imports marked noqa: PLC0415). Better still, make Widgets/Console/__init__.py a PEP 562 lazy facade, following the Local_Ingestion template, so no consumer of one Console submodule pays for all 34.
fix_notes: A function-local import in _stage_library_prompt_for_console is the smallest and safest change, and it removes the whole delta (the stub run shows no other path pulls the package). Also check the TYPE_CHECKING and annotation uses of the two names, and any tests that monkeypatch library_screen.PromptVariablesDialog. A PEP 562 facade for Widgets/Console/__init__ is broader: tests and patch targets use tldw_chatbook.Widgets.Console.X, and the Chat first-paint census (_ui_ready) would shift. Do that as a separate change.
evidence:
library_screen.py:301  from ...Widgets.Console.prompt_variables_dialog import (
    PromptVariablesDialog, PromptVariablesDialogRequest,)
# used only at 26963/26990 (_stage_library_prompt_for_console)
Widgets/Console/__init__.py: 34 eager `from .console_* import` lines (console_context_controls, console_project_instructions -> Chat.console_chat_controller, ...)
reason: library_screen.py:301 imports Widgets.Console.prompt_variables_dialog at module scope. It is used only at 26963 and 26990 (_stage_library_prompt_for_console). Importing it runs Widgets/Console/__init__.py, which has around 34 eager console_* imports and pulls in Chat.console_chat_controller. No backlog task covers it: the grep for prompt_variables_dialog and Console/__init__ found only Done or unrelated tasks, and TASK-22503 is the Library package, not Widgets/Console. On the default chat-first boot (config default_tab = 'chat', config.py:3713) the Console package is already loaded, so the marginal cost is zero there. The cost lands on Library-first boots (default_tab library or search) and on the background pre-importer thread.

title: Entry reconcile builds a throwaway replacement canvas (and its state) even when the mounted canvas is synced in place, so list state is built twice per reconcile
trigger: Yes, but low frequency. It runs once per presentation-changing snapshot: a visit resume, a completed ingest job, or a note save.
cost: Estimated, not measured: one extra list-state build (a sort over at most 100 records) plus one unmounted widget construction per reconcile. Roughly 1 ms, well below hot-path thresholds.
fix: Probe the mounted canvas first with query_one+NoMatches or _library_layout_ref, and only build the replacement widget and its state on the replacement branch. Pass the already-built state into _sync_library_canvas instead of rebuilding it.
fix_notes: Keep _adopt_library_conversation_state_selection running on both branches, because the sync path relies on the adopted selection. The error-surface branch (was_mounted / expected_selector reset) mutates expected_selector before the probe. Reorder carefully so the probe still sees the final selector.
evidence:
12575 conversations_state = self._build_library_conversations_state()
12580 replacement = LibraryConversationsCanvas(conversations_state, ...)
12603 replacement = LibraryNotesCanvas(**self._library_notes_list_canvas_kwargs(), ...)  # builds+sorts notes list state
12655 if expected_selector and self.query(expected_selector):   # mounted -> _sync_library_canvas(...) rebuilds state; replacement discarded
reason: In _reconcile_library_entry_state (library_screen.py:12505), each list branch builds its replacement widget and state before the mounted-canvas probe. That covers conversations (12575 builds state, 12580 the canvas), notes (LibraryNotesCanvas(**_library_notes_list_canvas_kwargs()), which builds and sorts the list state), prompts and skills. When `expected_selector and self.query(expected_selector)` (~12655) is true, _sync_library_canvas rebuilds the state and the replacement is discarded. The kwargs builders have no consuming side effects: the skills list uses consume_scroll=False. One exception: the conversations branch's _adopt_library_conversation_state_selection is a required side effect.

title: Per-visit source snapshot pulls full note bodies (SELECT *) the list never shows, then deep-copies and deep-compares the whole snapshot on the loop
trigger: Yes. It runs once per ScreenResume and once per completed ingest job, when not suspended.
cost: Not re-measured. deepcopy of str objects is identity, so body size adds almost nothing to the loop-side copy. The main costs are about 0.5 ms of dict copying and O(total body length) string equality in the compare. Retained memory is bounded at 100 bodies, so this is hygiene-grade.
fix: Use a list-shaped notes query (id, title, created/last_modified, keywords, version) for the snapshot. Store the snapshot as immutable tuples or MappingProxyType so the cache write and seed need no deepcopy, or at least move the clone into the worker thread.
fix_notes: Before dropping 'content', grep for any path that seeds note detail or instant-open from list records, or that matches the Search/RAG or notes filter on body text. None was found in library_notes_state.py, but the untruncated repo-wide consumer hunt was not exhaustive. The deepcopy exists to isolate the app-level cache from screen mutation (patch_note_records_after_save and the in-place record patches in the notes controller). Switching to immutable records requires converting those mutators.
evidence:
13316 self._run_library_service_call(list_notes, scope="local_note", limit=LIBRARY_SOURCE_PAGE_SIZES["notes"] (100), ...)
  -> ChaChaNotes_DB._list_generic_items: "SELECT * FROM notes WHERE deleted = 0 ORDER BY ..."  (content included)
11438 snapshot = clone_library_source_snapshot((records, ...))   # copy.deepcopy on the loop
12899 normalized_records != self._local_source_records           # deep equality of all rows
reason: The snapshot calls NotesScopeService.list_notes, which goes to NotesInteropService.list_notes, then CharactersRAGDB.list_notes, then _list_generic_items: 'SELECT * FROM notes WHERE deleted = 0 ORDER BY last_modified DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?', content included. The DB leg runs isolate_in_worker=True (off-loop). On the loop, clone_library_source_snapshot deep-copies the result (library_screen.py:11438) and the rows are deep-compared (12899). Among the consumers of _local_source_records['notes'], build_library_notes_list_state, sort and title lookup, none reads 'content'. Only detail normalisation (library_notes_state.py:871) does, and it takes the detail fetch.

title: _run_library_service_call(isolate_in_worker=True) creates and tears down a fresh asyncio event loop per call
trigger: Yes, but off the UI loop. The calls happen a few times per visit and per item open.
cost: Measured in a worker thread: asyncio.run() median 0.22 ms, p95 0.47 ms, against 0.045 ms for a reused asyncio.Runner. This is about 1 ms of worker latency per visit and adds nothing to the event loop.
fix: Call a sync twin of these scope methods directly in the worker. Alternatively, drive the coroutine with a cached per-thread asyncio.Runner instead of asyncio.run per call.
fix_notes: A per-thread cached Runner on to_thread's default executor threads keeps one event loop alive per pool thread across calls. Any service coroutine that creates loop-bound primitives (asyncio.Lock, clients cached on the loop) would then leak state between calls. It would also bypass run_finite_local_worker's per-call finiteness contract unless the Runner is created inside it. Calling a sync twin of the scope methods directly is cleaner, but it duplicates the policy-enforcement path (_enforce_policy) the async methods run. Low value; hygiene only.
reason: _run_library_service_call (library_screen.py:12995-13024) is confirmed: with isolate_in_worker=True it runs invoke_service_in_worker through asyncio.to_thread, and that calls asyncio.run() once per call whenever the service returns an awaitable. The code marks this with a deliberate 'policy-exception: worker-thread loop' comment. There are 26 isolate_in_worker=True sites in library_screen.py and 49 in Library_Modules. The per-call sqlite connection close is the separate, already-known TASK-24457 (8 fresh connections per visit).

title: Roleplay library remounts every row on each debounced search keystroke, page, sort and refresh; Dictionaries/Lore are unpaged
trigger: Per Roleplay visit (initial load), per mode switch, per debounced search pause, per page/sort/tag change, and after character mutations. All run on the event loop through awaited mounts.
cost: Re-measured with a minimal Textual 8.2.8 app at 211x44. clear+extend of 50 rows (200 widgets) took 43-74 ms for the mount alone and 115-153 ms including a pilot.pause (the pause has about 45-90 ms of fixed overhead: N=10 measured 47-96 ms). Real loop cost is about 50-100 ms per render, before the app's large stylesheet, which may raise it. That is above the P1 threshold on a per-visit/per-search path. Dictionaries/Lore are unpaged, but realistic counts are small, so that half only matters with large data.
fix: Stop remounting. Keep PERSONAS_LIBRARY_PAGE_SIZE row widgets and update their Static text, classes and ids in place, or diff by dom_id (remove only the missing rows, mount only the new ones). Short-circuit when the new rows tuple equals the last one rendered. Page the Dictionaries/Lore modes like Characters, and filter the cached _dictionaries_cache/_lore_books_cache in memory for search.
fix_notes: Textual forbids changing a widget's id once set (dom.py raises "Node 'id' attribute may not be changed once set"). The suggested 'update ids in place' is therefore impossible. Use fixed slot ids (row-0..row-49) with _row_lookup keyed by slot, or diff by dom_id (remove missing, mount new, move_child to reorder). Preserve _marked_ids pruning, mark_active_row, the ListView index/highlight, and the recovery/empty-row branches. The cheapest first step is a short-circuit when the rows tuple and pagebar args equal the last render. Filtering _dictionaries_cache/_lore_books_cache in memory on search is safe, since only mutations need a re-fetch.

# personas_library_pane.py:419-482
