... item = ListItem(Vertical(Static(name_text), Static(row.meta)), id=dom_id, ...)
await list_view.extend(items)
reason: Checked on 840ed2ca58. personas_library_pane.py:419 runs `await list_view.clear()` and :482 runs `await list_view.extend(items)`. Each row is a new ListItem(Vertical(Static, Static)), so 4 widgets per row. update_rows has no equality short-circuit. Callers: _display_character_page:3690 (page_size=PERSONAS_LIBRARY_PAGE_SIZE=50), dictionaries:4327 and lore:4409 (no page_size, all rows), plus :3719, :4021, :4526 and :4541. The search path is debounced (0.2 s set_timer at :4072 with cancel, then an exclusive run_worker, then _render_search_query), so it fires once per typing pause, not per key; the finder said so correctly. Sort cycle (_cycle_sort), tag filter (_apply_tag_filter), page delta (_on_page_changed_delta) and mode switch all call _reload_active_library and then update_rows. TASK-112 (debounce) is Done, and no open task covers the remount.

title: vLLM setup calls get_api_key, and therefore a ~13 ms load_settings() admission handshake, on every keystroke and 4 Hz during probes
trigger: Every accepted keystroke in any vLLM setup text field, and every 0.25 s during a vLLM launch probe.
cost: Not re-run, because load_settings touches profile paths. The mechanism is identical to the guarded bootstrap that TASK-32804.1 measured at 4.8-11 ms warm, and TASK-32804.3 measured ~49 ms for 6 admissions. The finder's 12.8-13 ms is consistent with that. So each keystroke costs about 5-13 ms on the loop. Under contention the handshake can also wait on _config_file_lock held by a config writer, so the stall is unbounded in that case. The same hit-path tax applies to all 103 `load_settings()` call sites.
fix: In this slice: compute credential_configured once, after profiles load or on a config-changed event, and cache it on the screen. Alternatively, derive it from app_instance.app_config['api_settings']['vllm'] plus the env var through resolve_provider_api_key, so apply_state stays cheap. Root fix (config.py): serve load_settings' _cache_hit before entering @_config_participants.guarded, the same way TASK-32804.1's _warm_config_cache_hit does for load_cli_config_and_ensure_existence, so only _load_settings_uncached pays admission. TASK-32804.1 left load_settings guarded on the hit path, so this is new scope.
fix_notes: The root fix mirrors 32804.1. Do not rebind load_settings, because guarded's wrapper checks `getattr(source, name) is wrapped` and 'load_settings' is in its allowed set. Instead, drop @guarded from load_settings, serve _cache_hit() first, and keep the guard on _load_settings_uncached (already in the allowed set), or add a guarded inner. Also check the TASK-32804.1 pin test and the storage-admission tests. The local fix (caching credential_configured on the screen) risks stale readiness after a key is saved in Settings or an env change, so invalidate it on config-publish or on screen resume.
evidence:
# llm_screen.py:3310-3324
@on(VllmSetupView.DraftChanged)
def _on_vllm_draft_changed(self, event): ... self._apply_vllm_view_state(focus=False)
# llm_screen.py:2837 (inside _apply_vllm_view_state)
    credential_configured=bool(get_api_key("vllm")),
# config.py:1861  @_config_participants.guarded  def load_settings(...)  (cache hit still inside the guard)
# config.py:9345  settings = load_settings()   # in get_api_key
reason: Chain verified. In vllm_setup_view.py (tldw_chatbook/UI/LLM_Management/, not UI/Screens), @on(Input.Changed) at :1589 maps every vLLM field to _change_draft (:1472) or _change_numeric_lexeme (:1484). Both post DraftChanged (:1482/:1499). LLMScreen._on_vllm_draft_changed (llm_screen.py:3310) then runs _apply_vllm_view_state, which calls `credential_configured=bool(get_api_key("vllm"))` at :2837. get_api_key (config.py:9319) calls load_settings() at :9345. load_settings is decorated with @_config_participants.guarded (config.py:1862), and its `_cache_hit()` check is INSIDE the guarded body. guarded's wrapper (config_participants.py:400-420) always enters operation(). That builds a storage._Acquisition and takes _settings_rebuild_lock + _config_file_lock (polling at 0.05 s) plus raw._scope, even on a warm hit. Nothing rebinds load_settings to a fast path; the only warm fast path is _warm_config_cache_hit, used by load_cli_config_and_ensure_existence. TASK-32804.1 (In Progress) fixed only that path. Its AC#2 ('handshake amortised per derivation rather than paid per read') is unmet for load_settings, and TASK-32804.3 separately measured ~8 ms per load_settings admission. This is new scope under 32804.1. The _probe_vllm_generation loop also calls _apply_vllm_view_state every 0.25 s (:4044), and there are 47 call sites of _apply_vllm_view_state.

title: Meetings transcript repaints the whole RichLog on every relabelled segment: O(n^2) per meeting, with bursts at Stop
trigger: Only with live_diarization enabled. One full repaint per diarizer-assigned segment while recording, a burst of k repaints at Stop (the batch diarize relabel), and one per rename.
cost: Re-measured RichLog(wrap=True) clear plus rewrite at 211x44 with ~110-char lines: 100 lines 6-13 ms, 360 lines 22-33 ms, 720 lines 47-64 ms. During recording that is one 20-60 ms hitch per segment late in a long meeting. A Stop pass relabelling hundreds of segments serializes roughly k x 30-60 ms of loop work, i.e. seconds of sluggish UI.
fix: Coalesce repaints. In _render_segment, set a dirty flag and schedule one _repaint_log through call_after_refresh or set_timer(0.1) if none is pending, so each frame gets at most one repaint. Have the Stop pass emit a single batch ('segments') event instead of one per segment. Longer term, render lines as per-line Statics in a VerticalScroll (update only the changed one) or cap RichLog history.
fix_notes: Coalescing is the low-risk fix: set a dirty flag and schedule one _repaint_log via call_after_refresh or set_timer if none is pending. rendered_lines stays authoritative, so the _rendered_transcript_text test hook is unaffected. A batch 'segments' event changes the session emit and sink contract (the sinks persist per seq), so it is a medium-risk change; keep it separate.
reason: Code verified. meetings_screen.py:836-843: when a re-delivered segment's line changes, _render_segment calls _repaint_log, which does `log.clear()` and then rewrites every line of rendered_lines (:846-850). meeting_session.py:889 emits each segment, and :924 re-emits it after _diarizer.assign sets speaker_id; the label changes from coarse to 'Speaker N', so each assigned segment costs a full repaint. The Stop pass re-emits every relabelled segment one at a time (:791-793). Each emit goes through _on_session_event, then a blocking app.call_from_thread(_apply_event), then a full repaint, so the cost is O(k*n). _rerender_transcript (:996) repaints for renames and self-match. BUT the whole path needs self._diarizer, which exists only when `[meetings] live_diarization` is on, and that defaults to false (config.py:5540; meeting_owner.py:174/560). The claim that _attach_if_running replays segments into repaints is overstated: replayed lines that are unchanged hit neither branch, and new ones append. Downgraded from P1: this is an opt-in feature, and the cost only scales with long meetings.

title: Lore list counts entries with an N+1 query that loads every entry's content, repeated per search keystroke and per entry edit
trigger: Lore mode entry, each debounced lore search pause, and every lore book/entry mutation (11 _render_lore_rows call sites).
cost: Estimated, off the event loop. It costs 1+B transactions (each taxed by the TASK-31502 quiescence registry) plus a full decode of every entry of every book. That is negligible for typical data (a few books) and tens of ms of worker time with GIL contention for about 50 books x 100 entries. This is a data-scaling N+1 on a less-frequent path, so P2.
fix: Get the counts in one statement: a LEFT JOIN or GROUP BY in list_world_books (SELECT world_book_id, COUNT(*) FROM world_book_entries WHERE deleted=0 GROUP BY world_book_id), or a count_world_book_entries() helper. For search, filter the cached _lore_books_cache/_dictionaries_cache in memory; only mutations need a re-fetch.
fix_notes: The proposed SQL is wrong: world_book_entries has NO `deleted` column (schema in ChaChaNotes_DB.py:1824 and recovery_core_schema.py:348). Use `SELECT world_book_id, COUNT(*) FROM world_book_entries GROUP BY world_book_id` (idx_world_book_entries_book exists), or a LEFT JOIN count in list_world_books. Per CLAUDE.md, capture a query plan without sqlite_stat1 if the query shape changes. The in-memory search filter over _lore_books_cache is safe.
reason: personas_screen.py:4354-4359: _list_world_books_with_counts calls manager.list_world_books(True), then runs `len(manager.get_world_book_entries(book['id']))` per book. world_book_manager.py:538-586: each call is its own db.transaction() with SELECT keys, content, ... and 3 json.loads per entry, only for len(). It runs off-loop via asyncio.to_thread (:4381). It is called from _render_lore_rows, which always re-fetches, including on a debounced search (:4209). _lore_books_cache is written but not used for filtering. It also runs after lore entry reload (:6607) and 11 call sites in total. No open task covers it.

title: One character selection reads the same SELECT * character_cards row (with image BLOB) 5 times over serial thread hops
trigger: Every local character selection in Roleplay (click/Enter, first-paint auto-select, restore, CharacterCardChanged reload).
cost: Estimated. Each read copies the portrait BLOB (a 1-2 MB memcpy is about 0.1-0.2 ms) and deserializes the JSON fields, which is larger when a card embeds a lorebook. That is about 1-3 ms per read, so roughly 5-15 ms of redundant worker time per selection, plus 3 serial thread hops of added latency. It does not freeze the UI.
fix: Load the card once, in one to_thread call or by reusing the handler's load result, and fan the record out to pure helpers: _embedded_dictionaries(record), _embedded_character_world_books(record), and record['image'] for the avatar and the eligibility check. Run the remaining independent steps concurrently with asyncio.gather.
fix_notes: Medium risk. The dictionary read goes through ChatDictionaryScopeService._invoke, which calls _enforce_policy and wraps the call in a Backup_Recovery _DictionaryJob admission. The actor-pack read goes through the @_chat_sources.guarded local service. title: Model install progress sends one UI event per 1 MiB chunk with no throttle, flooding the loop during pre-verify hashing
trigger: Every curated or remote model install. The pre-verify phase posts one message per MiB at hashing speed. The fetch phase posts at download speed, which is benign.
cost: Estimated. About 10 query_one plus 4 Static.update and 2 ProgressBar.update per event, roughly 0.3-1 ms. Hashing a page-cached file runs at about 0.5-2 GB/s, so 500-2000 events/s: loop saturation for the duration of pre-verify of a multi-GB model, plus backlog drain. Per-install, less-frequent path, so P2.
fix: Throttle in deliver(): forward only on a phase or file change, on the final byte, or when at least 100 ms have passed since the last forwarded event, and keep the latest progress in _model_install_last_progress for hydration. Use post_message or call_soon_threadsafe rather than blocking call_from_thread for progress.
fix_notes: Throttling in deliver() (on phase or file change, the final byte, or every >=100 ms) is low risk. Always forward the terminal event of each phase, and keep _model_install_last_progress updated for hydration. For audio_cpp, keep the cancel-event and is_attached check. Swapping call_from_thread for a non-blocking post is fine because post_message is already thread-safe, but preserve the deliver_current ownership check. Also note that the worker loop's to_thread completion is queued behind every pending progress callback.

# llm_screen.py:742-745: self.refresh_lab_status(); view.apply_progress(event.progress)

The fetch path's on_chunk (:1587) does the same per 1 MiB (fetch.py _CHUNK_BYTES=1 MiB at :33). No throttle exists in acquisition.py or fetch.py (a grep for throttl/monotonic found nothing). The only 64 MiB throttle is the local-copy path (service.py:126/3983). deliver (llm_screen.py:2099 curated, :4636 remote) calls _deliver_curated, which posts InstallProgressed to llm_window. The 0.25 s poll early-returns when not is_active but still wakes at 4 Hz; stop it in suspend and re-arm it on resume. Cancel the search debounce in suspend. Actor-pack export/import cancel and the preview gateway: decide whether an in-flight export should survive navigation, as Chat decided for runs. Follow the TASK-31520/31521 per-row on_unmount disposition audit.

title: New Actor Pack loads 256 character cards with portrait BLOBs into memory at once to build a picker
trigger: 'New Actor Pack' in Personas mode with a local runtime: personas_screen.py:7499 -> _begin_create_actor_pack (7603). User-initiated and infrequent.
cost: Estimated, not measured. The transient peak is roughly (number of cards with images, up to 256) × BLOB size plus the other deserialized card fields: about 75-500 MB for a large portrait library, far less for typical libraries. Off-thread latency is one PIL verify plus one SHA-256 per portrait (about 1-2 ms/MB), i.e. about 0.3-0.5 s before the picker opens at 256 × ~1 MB. It only scales with large data on a rare path, so P2 is right.

fix_notes: Prefer a narrow projection (id, name, version, image) in pages of ~16, validating and hashing as each page streams, so the peak is one page. The sha256 and revision are used later as the session's portrait fence (_ActorPackCreateSession.portrait_choices), so a lazy-validate-on-pick variant must still compute and fence them at pick time. It would also change UX: characters with invalid portraits would appear in the picker and fail later. Keep the eager filter, only paged. OFFSET paging over ORDER BY name is fine at 256. Unrelated correctness note: the limit=256 silently hides eligible characters beyond the first 256 by name.

title: Root cause (outside the slice): every ScheduledTasksDB operation starts a private-sqlite helper child process, 39-46 ms per call against 0.6 ms for plain sqlite
trigger: Every service.db.* call in the Schedules workbench (F1-F5), the scheduler loop, the sync engine, and any other store that opens per operation on macOS/Linux.
cost: Measured in an isolated scratch profile on this pin: `_get_connection`+close median 51 ms; list_task_runs 53.8 ms, get_sync_state 60.4 ms, count_unread_results 51.3 ms, get_conflicts 61.6 ms; a raw sqlite3 connect+query took 0.7 ms. A Popen counter recorded exactly 1 spawn per read (10/10). cProfile put prepare_in_helper at ~42 ms of the ~52 ms per open. Roughly 70x overhead per operation.
fix: Highest leverage: give ScheduledTasksDB a held per-thread connection, like the ClientNotificationsDB._held_connection template. The store's own docstring flags this as 'its own task': explicit BEGIN plus isolation_level=None, auditing the ~22 transaction() bodies. Alternatively, cache the helper's per-path preparation verdict by (dev, ino, mode) so repeat opens of an already-verified file skip the child process. Report this to the DB-layer slice as well, because any per-operation-connection store pays the same cost.
fix_notes: A held per-thread connection (the ClientNotificationsDB._held_connection template at client_notifications_db.py:163) is the safer lever. It must register with the Backup_Recovery participants (_register_core_connection/_core_access) so that maintenance or restore can close it, and the ~22 transaction() bodies need explicit BEGIN when switching to isolation_level=None, as the store docstring warns. The alternative of caching the helper's verdict by (dev, ino, mode) weakens a deliberate per-open security check (the helper validates without opening inodes locally, to avoid TOCTOU). Treat it as security-sensitive and needing owner sign-off, not a free perf win. Raise this with the DB-layer owner as an app-wide finding, because other per-operation stores pay the same cost.
reason: ScheduledTasksDB._get_connection (scheduled_tasks_db.py:215) calls BaseDB._get_connection (base_db.py:818), which calls connect_private_sqlite and then _connect_registered_sqlite (private_sqlite.py:1709). On every non-Windows file-backed open that calls prepare_in_helper (:1878), and HelperLease.start (private_sqlite_process.py:367) runs `subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '-I', '-S', private_sqlite_helper_entry.py])` per call. Nothing caches or reuses the helper per path; the only prepare_in_helper call site is :1878. The store deliberately opens a connection per operation (its docstring calls conversion 'its own task'). git log -S shows the helper-per-open arrived 2026-09-07 (61a49de2e0), after all the holistic perf reviews (08-22 to 09-04). TASK-24457 (Library, 8 connections, filed 08-29) predates it and prices only the PRAGMAs, and no backlog task mentions the helper spawn cost. connect_private_sqlite has 94 call sites repo-wide, so every per-operation-connection store pays this.

(2) Skip the second restart while a research-workspace-sources worker is still running. _refresh_source_workbench reads self._source_folders only at its final sync_workspace, after every await, so the in-flight worker will pick up the new folders anyway. title: Every Settings category switch re-mints both panes from scratch; heavy categories cost 215-900 ms of loop time, and a mount-echo Changed storm reruns the staging cascade
trigger: Yes. A rail click, j/k+Enter or search Enter goes through _select_category, sets active_category, and runs watch_active_category -> _swap_category_panes -> recompose of both panes on the loop. The worker is a coroutine, not a thread. The 25+ _refresh_settings_workspaces_pane callers use the same path.
cost:
Measured by the finder in an isolated real-app probe; I re-read the raw JSON. Loop-busy per switch:
- Heavy categories: 215-1346 ms, with max handle 80-620 ms. Part of this is gen2 GC, see F2.
- Light categories: 35-60 ms.

stylesheet.apply dominance comes from the finder's profile, which I did not re-run.
fix:
Three levers, in order of payoff:

(a) Cache per-category panes instead of recomposing on every switch. Use a ContentSwitcher (or a dict of SettingsRegion children) keyed by category: mount a category on its first visit, toggle display afterwards, and recompose only when that category's data actually changed (after save/revert, workspace mutations). This is the same pattern as TASK-24452's reuse.

(b) Lazy-compose Collapsible bodies and gated rows on first expand instead of minting hidden subtrees.

(c) Kill the mount-echo storm. Have the _stage_* helpers return whether the draft changed, and early-return from _mark_*_staged / _persist_* when nothing changed and the draft was already clean. Alternatively, mount controls under prevent(Input.Changed, Select.Changed, Checkbox.Changed) and seed state explicitly.
fix_notes:
Lever (a), per-category pane caching with ContentSwitcher, is riskier than stated:
- Collides with shared per-category widget ids. _render_impact_pane_header (:22438) yields id="settings-selected-category-draft-status" for every category, and the state banner (:9717) is also per category. With several cached panes mounted, the many query_one("#...") calls (for example _update_draft_status_widgets at :9056) would hit a hidden category's copy.
- Raises the live widget count, which the finder shows makes per-key cost worse.

Safer order: (c) first, then (b), then (a).

On (c): screen.prevent() around the region recompose will not catch Select echoes, because those are posted from each Select's own _on_mount in its own pump. A value-equality early return in the _stage_*/_mark_* helpers is safer. Some handlers deliberately rely on the constructor echo (the _model_catalog_form_values comment at :15174), so audit that before suppressing.

title: gen2 GC pauses of 120-360 ms land every 1-2 Settings category switches; the app never calls gc.freeze() after boot
trigger: Yes. The allocation churn comes from F1's pane re-mint (100-400 widgets per switch), and a gen2 lands inside whatever loop handle is running at the time. That explains 169-331 ms max handles on light categories such as tool-profiles, watchlists and diagnostics.
cost: Measured by the finder (gc.callbacks timing around the probe); I re-read catgc.json. gen2: 96-356 ms per collection, about 3.46 s over 61 transitions. I corrected the frequency to about every 3-4 switches.
fix: Call gc.freeze() once after _ui_ready (and optionally after the screen pre-importer finishes). This moves the boot heap into the permanent generation, so gen2 scans only post-boot objects. Per TASK-31966 AC#2 this global GC policy change needs an ADR. Pair it with F1 so there is less churn to collect. New evidence for TASK-31966: its scope is Console activation, but Settings reproduces the same pauses on every 1-2 category switches.
fix_notes:
gc.freeze() after boot is a global GC policy change, and TASK-31966 AC#2 requires an approved ADR first.

CPython 3.12 caveats:
- After freeze, long_lived_total counts only unfrozen objects, so the 25% full-collection ratio fires more often. The collections are cheaper, but the net effect must be measured.
- Any garbage cycle frozen at boot is never reclaimed.

Pair the change with F1's churn reduction, and check the round-over-round growth before attributing it all to heap size.

title: Trajectory search re-renders the whole ledger synchronously on every keystroke, including a full-trace json.dumps/lower() match pass
trigger: Every Input.Changed in #trajectory-search on the TrajectoryScreen, which is pushed from the Console review-selection trace launch (UI/Console_Modules/wiring.py:497-510). Also n/p and error/tool/feedback jumps via _navigate_records, filter-bar changes and turn toggles. Only while the trace screen is open.
cost: Measured. Match pass over 2000 records: ~1.6 ms at 1 KiB and ~13 ms at 8 KiB. Live results are capped at ~2 KB, so ~3 ms is realistic. DataTable clear+re-add of 500 rows: ~5 ms synchronous, plus ~65-75 ms of layout/paint (bare app). Typing into a trace of 500+ records therefore costs ~70-80 ms per keystroke, dominated by the table rebuild, not by json.dumps/lower.
fix: (1) Debounce the search input about 150 ms, using the browser-search cancellation-token pattern the repo already uses. (2) Precompute one lowercased search blob per record once per snapshot (preview + kind + model + provider + name + json args + result), keyed by record key, and match with a single `in`. (3) Compute the match set once per render and reuse it for both _turn_row_specs and update_counts instead of calling _matching_records() again. (4) Above about 1k records, route search renders through the existing _render_worker thread path with render generations.
fix_notes: Debouncing (~150 ms, cancellation-token pattern) is the main lever, because the table rebuild dominates. Passing the already-computed match set into update_counts removes the duplicate full scan (1286). A precomputed lowercased blob helps much less than claimed, since live results are ≤2 KB. If adopted, build it lazily per snapshot keyed by record key and drop it on snapshot swap, or it doubles payload memory for legacy large-payload traces. Routing search renders through _render_worker is viable because the generation guard already exists, but _build_row_specs reads screen state (_collapsed, _query, filter state) from the thread. Snapshot those inputs first. Diffing rows instead of clear+re-add would cut the paint cost further.
evidence:
def on_input_changed(self, event):  # 1607
    self._query = event.value.strip()
    self._render_ledger()            # no debounce
...args_text = json.dumps(args, sort_keys=True)   # 1200, per record per key
...if result is not None and query in str(result).lower():  # 1206, full untruncated result
...table.clear(columns=False)  # 1250, then add_row x up to 500+
...len(self._matching_records()),  # 1286, re-matches ALL records, not just the window
reason: Code verified at trajectory_screen.py:1607-1612: on_input_changed calls _render_ledger with no debounce. _render_ledger calls _apply_row_specs(_build_row_specs()) synchronously. _build_row_specs matches only the mounted window (_flat_slice, at most PAGE_SIZE=500). _apply_row_specs then calls table.clear (1250), re-adds every row, and at 1286 runs _matching_records() a second time over ALL records just to get a count. _navigate_records (1832) also rescans all records for n/p/error/tool/feedback jumps. Launch path: wiring.py:_present_console_trajectory pushes TrajectoryScreen. It is an occasional diagnostic screen, not a common path, and its cost only grows with large traces, so P2, not P1. The finder's cost basis is inflated for live traces. Console tool results reach the trace through console_chat_store._trajectory_tool_payload -> redact_log_line(raw_result), whose default cap is MAX_REDACTED_LINE_CHARS=2000 (in place since 6c41c7435b, 2026-08-22). Agent-step records omit args and result entirely (trajectory.py:1225-1240). So 8 KiB+ results exist only in legacy pre-cap rows or foreign imported bundles. My micro-benchmark of lower()+`in` over 2000 payloads: 1.6 ms at 1 KiB, 13.1 ms at 8 KiB, 51.8 ms at 32 KiB, so realistic live payloads cost only ~3 ms for the match pass. The dominant real per-keystroke cost is the DataTable rebuild. In a bare Textual 8.2.8 app at 211x44, clear plus 500 add_row took 4-5 ms, and the following layout/paint added ~65-75 ms over an idle-pause baseline (~28 ms extra for 50 rows).

title: Video player converts full-resolution frames and builds the image renderable on the UI thread at 24 fps; ffmpeg emits native-resolution rgb24
trigger: UI/Console_Modules/video.py:1305-1307 and 1501-1504 push VideoPlayerScreen from a Console video card. For the whole playback, _pump_loop hands every frame to the UI thread at PLAYER_TARGET_FPS=24 (player_pipeline.py:38).
cost: Measured the PIL portion: ~0.8 ms frombytes plus ~1.1 ms thumbnail per 1080p frame (halfcell), and ~12.7 ms resize+PNG+b64 for the kitty-equivalent work, before the synchronous stdout write and the Textual paint. At 24 fps that is roughly 30%+ of the loop in kitty mode and a few percent in halfcell/ascii, plus ~149 MB/s of pipe traffic at 1080p.
fix: Add a scale step to the ffmpeg filter chain that targets the render box, e.g. `fps=24,scale=W:H:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease` with W/H derived from the cell count x cell pixel size, or 80x80 for halfcell. That cuts pipe bytes and all PIL work by about 100x. Do the frombytes/thumbnail/Pixels.from_image/frame_to_ascii work in the pump thread and bridge only the finished renderable. For kitty, pass a pre-sized image so TGP skips its resize, and consider a lower fps cap or raw (f=24) transmission instead of PNG encoding.
fix_notes: An ffmpeg scale filter (fps=24,scale=W:H:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease) is the biggest single win. W/H must come from the cell count x textual_image get_cell_size(), and a terminal resize then needs a pipeline respawn or a conservative fixed box. Moving frombytes/thumbnail/Pixels.from_image/frame_to_ascii into the pump thread is safe, since they are pure. For kitty, the TGP renderable does its scale+PNG+b64 inside __rich_console__ on the loop wherever the Image is constructed. Pre-sizing only removes the resize step, so raw (f=24/32) transmission or pre-encoding is needed to move the rest. Also note that each frame allocates a new TGP terminal image id and cleanup() is never called, so images accumulate terminal-side until the terminal evicts them. Freeing the previous id per frame would fix that.
evidence:
dispatched = self._bridge(self._render_frame, token, pipeline, run, data)  # call_from_thread per frame
...image = PILImage.frombytes("RGB", (probe.width, probe.height), data)  # 6.2 MB at 1080p
TGPImage(image, width=PIXELS_MAX_COLS, height=PIXELS_MAX_LINES)  # kitty: resize+PNG+b64 at render
scaled = image.copy(); scaled.thumbnail(...); Pixels.from_image(scaled)  # halfcell
# player_pipeline.py: "-vf", f"fps={self._target_fps:g}"  -- no scale filter
reason: Code verified. video_player_screen.py:_pump_loop (thread worker) calls self._bridge(self._render_frame, ...) per frame (292), and _bridge uses app.call_from_thread, which is synchronous. _render_frame (310-352) does PILImage.frombytes on native-resolution rgb24 (327). Kitty mode builds a textual_image TGP Image (332). Its __rich_console__, run at paint on the loop, calls _send_image_to_terminal -> PixelData.scaled(...).to_base64(), i.e. resize, PNG encode and base64, then writes and flushes the whole payload synchronously to sys.__stdout__. PixelData also copies the full frame on construction. Halfcell does copy()+thumbnail()+Pixels.from_image on the loop (339-343). player_pipeline.py:264 is `-vf fps=24` with no scale filter, so ffmpeg pipes native-resolution frames. My benchmark at 1920x1080: frombytes 0.8 ms, copy+thumbnail 1.1 ms, and resize to 800x800+PNG+b64 12.7 ms on a smooth gradient frame. That is consistent with the finder's 24 ms kitty figure on realistic frames. Because call_from_thread blocks the pump, frames are dropped rather than queued, so loop occupancy is render cost x 24 fps: ~30-60% of the loop in kitty mode for the whole playback. It is not on a common path, but it is a per-tick cost sustained for the entire playback, so P1 stands. No backlog task covers it; task-3401.10 is the Done feature task.

title: Trajectory live refresh and sub-5000-record mounts rebuild keys, filters, timeline and the whole ledger synchronously on the UI thread
trigger: TrajectoryScreen open over the Console with a revision_provider (review_selection.py:626 lambda: store.get_payload_revision(conv_id)). Any payload-revision bump (message append/complete/content update, variant ops, trajectory row writes) triggers one on-loop apply per 0.5 s tick. The first mount of any trace up to 5000 records is also synchronous.
cost: I did not re-measure the finder's 20.5 ms apply at 2000 records, but the per-record work (json.dumps+sha256, plus asdict deep copies for legacy rows) makes it plausible. On top of it, the DataTable clear+re-add of up to 500 rows measured ~5 ms synchronous plus ~65-75 ms layout/paint in a bare app. Each revision tick on a 500+ record trace can therefore cost well over 50 ms, up to twice per second.
fix: _live_rebuild_worker is already a thread, so build the row specs (and record keys) there and hand _apply_row_specs(specs, generation) the finished specs, the way _render_worker does. Lower WORKER_THRESHOLD to about 1,000 or always use the worker for mount. Skip set_records/set_snapshot when the snapshot's record count and last event id are unchanged.
fix_notes: _rebuild_record_keys both reads and mutates self._legacy_key_assignments. To move it to the worker, compute from a copied assignment map and commit the result on the loop under the revision guard, or two overlapping workers can diverge. Do not skip set_records/set_snapshot on unchanged count + last event id alone: message edits and variant changes bump the revision without changing either, and would leave stale previews or variants. Key the skip on the revision or on a content hash. Building specs in the worker should reuse _render_worker's generation guard.

reason: Code verified. _poll_revision (728) runs every 0.5 s (set_interval at 472) and hands off to _live_rebuild_worker (thread), which calls self.app.call_from_thread(self._apply_live_snapshot, ...). _apply_live_snapshot (785-864) runs on the loop. Its _rebuild_record_keys (801, body 534+) walks every record. After that come _filter_bar.set_records (options_from over all records), _timeline.set_snapshot with a dict comprehension over all records, and _render_ledger (847), which skips the WORKER_THRESHOLD check (108), so even a >5000-record trace re-renders synchronously on every revision. get_payload_revision is bumped by 52 store sites, including _update_message_content, _mark_message_complete, _append_message and write_trajectory_rows, so during an active run with the trace open the full 2 Hz poll rate is reachable. The mount path renders synchronously up to 5000 records (459-465). It is limited to the trace screen being open during a run, and scales with trace size, so P2.

Any inline truncation should cover variants too. Coalescing highlight-driven refreshes to one per frame is low risk.

The early return must still apply when current is None: visibility and model changes reset it to None to force a repaint. It must also not skip the clone-setup sync when the model select changed, although the model-change path already nulls the observation. Comparing the card projection is the more robust gate if diagnostics churn.

title: Fixed asyncio.sleep 'barriers' add 200 ms to every Play and 100 ms to every Pause/Resume
trigger: Every Play (button, keyboard action, auto-play after generation) and every Pause/Resume press in the Speech Playground.
cost: By inspection (fixed constants): +200 ms before audio starts on each Play, and +100 ms before each Pause/Resume takes effect. There are also 2 debug-only get_state() executor round trips per Play on a single-thread executor.
fix: Delete the fixed sleeps and the debug-only get_state() calls, and keep the awaited stop()/_retire_progress_timer() as the barrier. Make the debug logs lazy with logger.opt(lazy=True), or drop the .exists() call from the f-string. Verify on the macOS and Linux player backends that play() right after an awaited stop() is race-free.
fix_notes: Removing the 0.2 s sleep looks safe given stop()'s process.wait and the identity-guarded monitor. Verify with the mpv/ffplay/afplay backends that the audio device is released on exit, which matters for device-exclusive backends on Linux. Removing the post-play 0.1 s sleep narrows the window in which a Pause's exclusive worker cancels the Play worker, a correctness side-benefit. The :1309 unmount sleep should become an awaited cancel, not a sleep; tier-2 S21 made the same point.
evidence:
await self._retire_progress_timer()
# Small delay to ensure clean state
await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
state_after_stop = await self.app.audio_player.get_state()   # debug-only executor hop
...
# _pause_audio_async: Small delay to ensure UI is ready
await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
reason: The code matches. _play_audio_async runs `await asyncio.sleep(0.2)` (speech_playback_mixin.py:718) after an awaited audio_player.stop() and _retire_progress_timer(), before play(). That is 200 ms of pure added latency on every Play, whether from the button, action_play_audio or auto-play (callers at :208, :295, :1150). _pause_audio_async sleeps 0.1 s before acting (:786). There is a further post-play sleep(0.1) at :770, which does not delay audio but holds the exclusive 'stts-playback' worker, and on_unmount sleeps 0.05 s (:1309). I checked whether the barrier is really needed. AsyncAudioPlayer.stop runs in the executor and does process.kill()/terminate() plus process.wait(timeout) (audio_player.py:561-596), so the old process has exited when stop() returns. _monitor_playback only writes state when `self._current.process is process` (identity-guarded), so a late monitor thread cannot clobber the new playback. The sleep is redundant. These are asyncio sleeps, not loop blocks, so the cost is action latency, not a freeze.

title: 10 Hz playback progress loop does 3 thread hops and a layout-forcing label update per tick
trigger: Runs for the full duration of every Playground playback at 10 Hz.
cost: Not measured. Estimated at 30 executor round trips per second plus one small layout pass per tick while audio plays. Bounded to playback, so P3.
fix: Fetch the duration once when playback starts, and read state and position in a single executor call. Update the time label only when its text changes, with update(..., layout=False). Cache widget references. Consider a 4–5 Hz cadence.
fix_notes: Safe. Fetch the duration once, write the label only when its text changes, and optionally batch state+position into one executor call. Use layout=False only if the label's width is fixed by CSS; otherwise just skipping unchanged text is enough.

    position = await self.app.audio_player.get_position()
    duration = await self.app.audio_player.get_duration()

Each tick makes 3 awaited run_in_executor calls on the player's single-worker ThreadPoolExecutor (get_state, get_position, get_duration; audio_player.py:798-815), 3–4 query_one calls, ProgressBar.update, and time_display.update(), where #audio-time-display is a Static (speech_playground_pane.py:2944), so the update means refresh(layout=True). title: Small sync file I/O on the loop in Voice Blends and audio export handlers
trigger: Opening the Voice Blends view (STTS_Window view switch to 'blends' mounts VoiceBlendsPane, then on_mount). Clicking Add, Import or Export Voice Blends, handled by the mixin's on_button_pressed through the MRO. Clicking Export in the Playground, which calls _export_audio and then the FileSave callback. All are one-shot user actions, not per-keystroke or per-tick.
cost:
Estimated.
- Blend JSON is typically a few KB: sub-ms read and parse, plus an fsync on write of about 1-5 ms on macOS APFS.
- The import file is not size-capped, but realistic blend files are tiny.
- The WAV copy at Kokoro's 24 kHz 16-bit mono is about 2.9 MB per minute, so a 10-minute render is about 29 MB. That is roughly 10-30 ms for shutil.copy2 (fcopyfile) on SSD, once per export click.
- Nowhere near the 100 ms common-path P0 bar, and not a hot path.
fix: Run the blend read/merge/write and the export copy through asyncio.to_thread inside a worker. Build the blend list with ''.join(...). Cap the import file size.
fix_notes:
The export copy cannot simply move to a thread. handle_export calls release_artifact() in its `finally` (speech_playback_mixin.py:982-986), and that lease must be released only after the threaded copy finishes, so move the release into the worker's finally or the source artifact can be released mid-copy.

On threading generally:
- _handle_import_file and _handle_export_file are sync push_screen callbacks. Offloading them needs run_worker(thread=True) or @work(thread=True), with notify and _load_kokoro_voice_blends (which calls query_one) marshalled back via call_from_thread. Alternatively, make them async callbacks that await asyncio.to_thread for the I/O only.
- _show_add_voice_blend_dialog is already an async worker, so wrapping the read/merge/write in asyncio.to_thread is enough there.
- Keep the read-merge-write as one threaded unit so two quick imports cannot interleave.

The ''.join and size-cap items are optional hygiene and not worth doing on their own.

    self._load_kokoro_voice_blends()      # open + json.load + str += per blend
...
with open(import_path, "r") as f:
    imported_blends = json.load(f)        # user-picked file, unbounded
...
shutil.copy2(source_path, dest_path)     # FileSave callback, on the loop

- speech_settings_pane.py:265-266: VoiceBlendsPane.on_mount calls _load_kokoro_voice_blends. That does an exists() check, open and json.load of kokoro_ui_blend_file(), builds a string with += and runs query_one (mixin :844-876). The pane is mounted only when you switch the Speech view to 'blends' (STTS_Window.py:2049-2052, `await content_container.mount(VoiceBlendsPane(...))`).
- The mixin's on_button_pressed (:398-431) routes add-voice-blend-btn, import-blends-btn and export-blends-btn. Those buttons are composed live by VoiceBlendsPane through VOICE_BLEND_ACTIONS (pane :107-123, :254).

Import reads a user-picked file of any size, reads the blend file, then calls write_kokoro_ui_blends, which goes through atomic_private_write_text with os.fsync (private_paths.py:1401).
- _show_add_voice_blend_dialog (:1213-1237) is run_worker on a coroutine, which is not a thread, so its open/json.load/write+fsync also block the loop.
- speech_playback_mixin.py:1033: shutil.copy2 runs inside the FileSave callback handle_export (:982-986), reached from audio-export-btn (:305-306). It runs on the loop.

None of these are offloaded. No open task covers them: backlog greps for voice blend and Speech export turned up only Done tasks (1986, 15772). All are rare, user-initiated, non-hot paths, so P3 is right.

title: About 1.8k lines of dead legacy settings-form code are still shipped and mixed into live panes
trigger: speech_settings_contracts is on the boot import path: app.py:412 imports stts_events, which imports speech_settings_contracts at :82. speech_settings_mixin is imported with STTS_Window, which pulls in speech_settings_pane and then the mixin. The mixin's on_button_pressed runs through Textual's MRO dispatch on every Button.Pressed inside either pane. None of these is a hot path, and the dead methods themselves never execute.
cost:
Measured with an isolated `-X importtime` run: HOME, XDG_* and TLDW_CONFIG_PATH were pointed at scratch, with TLDW_TEST_MODE=1 and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1.
- speech_settings_mixin self-import is about 0.29-0.34 ms, once per process.
- speech_settings_contracts self-import is about 2.2-2.6 ms at boot. Rebuilding the whole 84-record SPEECH_TTS_OWNERSHIP_INVENTORY takes about 30 µs, and _build_ownership_index about 4.5 µs. So the ~2 ms is the live module's own class and dataclass definitions, and pruning the dead records would recover only tens of µs.
- speech_settings_group costs 0 at runtime.

The real cost is maintenance surface area, not speed. That makes it a P3 hygiene item.
fix: Delete speech_settings_group.py and its tests, and delete the unreachable legacy methods in SpeechSettingsMixin. Keep only the blend add/import/export and its _cli_setting/_tts_service_factory hooks, and move those into VoiceBlendsPane. Delete the overridden SpeechCatalogMixin._show_provider_specific_controls/_check_higgs_installation. Prune the dead control records from the ownership inventory.
fix_notes:
Before deleting the legacy SpeechSettingsMixin methods:
- Keep normalize_provider_voice_selection (mixin :70), which STTS_Window.py:1340 uses.
- Keep on_button_pressed's three blend branches plus the blend helpers, or move them into VoiceBlendsPane. SpeechSettingsPane.on_button_pressed deliberately defers blend ids to the inherited handler (:1545-1547), so that coupling breaks if the mixin handler is removed without moving the branches.
- Delete or port the tests that host the mixin and exercise _update_default_voice_options: Tests/UI/test_speech_kokoro_defaults.py:129, Tests/UI/test_stts_profile_library.py:1248 and Tests/TTS/test_local_provider_contracts.py:229. Also delete the two SpeechSettingsGroup tests.

Pruning the ownership inventory is a boot-path hazard. _build_ownership_index (contracts :573-601) raises ValueError at import if a record is missing from, or not listed in, speech_settings_model.ALL_SETTINGS_CONTROLS. That exception fires while app.py is importing stts_events, so it would crash boot. The inventory and ALL_SETTINGS_CONTROLS must be pruned in lockstep and checked with Tests/UI/test_speech_settings_contracts.py.

There is no measurable speed gain. Frame it as surface-area reduction, not a perf fix.

# SpeechSettingsMixin: legacy_on_mount, _set_initial_values, handle_default_selects_changed,

title: Left-rail WatchlistTree is fully rebuilt (plus sync source-row queries in compose) on every count refresh, including the debounced refresh after each article read
trigger: Yes. Opening any status=='new' item on the Read tab (j/k/click/space) leads to one rail+header rebuild 0.6 s after each reading pause. The same unconditional rail/header request fires after every tree-data load: visit, writes, scope reconciliation. Each expand, collapse or tag click also recomposes the whole tree through recompose=True reactives.
cost: Re-measured in an isolated headless run_test at 211x44 with default CSS. A 10-watchlist tree (62 widgets) rebuilds in 65.7 ms against a 22.8 ms pilot-pause baseline, about 43 ms net. With 3 watchlists expanded it is 67.4 ms. The instrumented loader ran 45 times over 15 rebuilds, i.e. one sync list_source_rows per expanded watchlist per rebuild, as claimed. This matches the finder's ~57 ms for 10 watchlists. The header/tab-strip rebuild comes on top of that. The result is a recurring ~50-100 ms stall on the primary reading loop, so P1 stands. It is borderline P0 only for large expanded trees.
fix: 1) Add WatchlistTree.apply_counts(counts, source_counts, unread_pin) that rewrites the affected Buttons' label/tooltip in place (ids are already deterministic: wl-tree-node-<kind>, wl-tree-node-watchlist-<id>, wl-tree-node-source-<occurrence>), and have _apply_tree_data_to_live_surfaces call it when the structural part of the snapshot (watchlists, all/unassigned source rows, tags) is unchanged -- only request _SURFACE_RAIL/_SURFACE_HEADER when structure changed. 2) Make expanded/expanded_root_kinds/active_tag non-recompose and mount/remove only the affected child rows after the toggled Horizontal. 3) Load expanded watchlists' source rows in the off-thread _read_tree_data_snapshot (it already calls service.list_sources for reconciliation) and pass them in, deleting the synchronous source_rows_loader from compose.
fix_notes: The in-place count path must treat one more case as STRUCTURAL: when the 'unread' aggregate root is expanded, its child rows are filtered by _source_counts[...]['unread'] > 0 (watchlist_tree.py compose, 'All Unread' node). Marking an item read can therefore remove a source row, which is more than a relabel. The signature must include the set of unread-positive source ids whenever 'unread' is in expanded_root_kinds, plus _unread_pin_source_id. Source badges switch between present and absent at 0, but that is still only a label change. _SURFACE_HEADER should likewise be requested only when the scoped summary inputs changed. Moving list_source_rows into _read_tree_data_snapshot needs list_source_rows (row dicts), not list_sources (ids only). Making expanded/active_tag non-recompose must preserve the TreeExpansionChanged/TreeTagFilterChanged watcher posts and the set_reactive seeding contract. Medium risk is fair.
evidence:
watchlist_tree.py:160  expanded: reactive[frozenset[int]] = reactive(frozenset(), recompose=True)  (+ expanded_root_kinds, active_tag, write/selection_disabled_reason)
watchlist_tree.py:654  self._source_cache[watchlist_id] = list(self._load_source_rows(watchlist_id))   # called from compose()
screen:2334 _load_source_rows_for_tree -> self._watchlist_bundle_service().list_source_rows(watchlist_id)  # 'Safe on the UI thread'
screen:1811 self._request_surface_refresh(self._SURFACE_RAIL, self._SURFACE_HEADER, self._SURFACE_INSPECTOR)  # unconditional per _load_tree_data
screen:12446 self._request_tree_counts_refresh()  # end of _mark_item_read_on_open, 0.6 s debounce -> _load_tree_data
reason: All cited lines match on 840ed2ca58 (tree reactives recompose=True at watchlist_tree.py:160-190; _source_rows cache at :654 lives on the instance; _build_tree_pane passes _load_source_rows_for_tree, whose docstring says it runs synchronously in compose). I traced the chain: _mark_item_read_on_open (screen:12381) ends with _request_tree_counts_refresh() (:12446). That re-arms a 0.6 s set_timer onto _load_tree_data (:1644). The snapshot read is off-loop via to_thread, but it then calls _apply_tree_data_to_live_surfaces, which always calls _request_surface_refresh(RAIL, HEADER, INSPECTOR) (:1809-1813). _drain_surface_refresh (:5025) then calls workbench.refresh_region_content(LEFT_RAIL) (watchlists_workbench.py:574). That builds a fresh WatchlistTree through the factory, removes the old one and mounts the new one. It also runs refresh_header_content, which rebuilds WatchlistsTabStrip plus the status markers and calls scoped_source_rows(). scoped_source_rows() issues a sync list_source_rows only when the scope is a watchlist or a watchlist-context source. The rail rebuild is skipped only when the LEFT_RAIL body is collapsed. Read needs 155 columns for all panes (region_layout.py), so at the owner's full-screen 211/235 widths the rail is always mounted. No debounce beyond the 0.6 s timer, no diffing and no cache survives the rebuild. That is arguably more correct than today, where each deepcopy freezes the patch state at copy time, but it is a semantic change and should be test-pinned. Shallow-copying only the newly admitted page (dict(row)) is sufficient.

title: Overview counts are computed by fetching 100 full item rows (with 2000-char previews) plus 100 runs/sources and all rules, sequentially
trigger: Screen visit (on_mount/backend switch) plus every deliberate write (source create/delete, check now, resume, OPML import, rule save/delete, status change). This runs in an exclusive async worker, and each read is an asyncio.to_thread hop.

The server backend has no item listing (it raises), so keep the current degraded path there. list_runs has no status parameter in either the local or the server service, so 'limit 10 + status filter' needs a new parameter in both. That change also alters semantics: it would return the 10 most recent failures overall instead of the failures among the last 100 runs. latest_run_status still needs the newest run of any status, so keep a separate limit=1 read. asyncio.gather is safe: file DBs use thread-local connections that each hop closes, in-memory DBs run inline, and the server path means only 3 concurrent HTTP calls. trigger: Every boot: tldw_chatbook.app -> Chat.console_display_state -> Utils.token_counter -> Utils.custom_tokenizers -> tokenizers (confirmed from importtime nesting). The tokenizers library is only used when the user has installed custom tokenizer mappings.
cost: Boot importtime: tokenizers cumulative 3.7 to 11.9 ms, and token_counter self time 2.8 to 3.0 ms (which includes the metadata scan). My probe: first metadata.version('tiktoken') call 1.48 ms max (0.2 ms median once warm), find_spec('tokenizers') 0.03 ms. The realistic saving is about 4 to 12 ms per boot, almost all from `tokenizers`.
fix: Set TOKENIZERS_AVAILABLE from importlib.util.find_spec('tokenizers') (0.06 ms) and import Tokenizer inside load_tokenizer/install_tokenizer. Use find_spec('tiktoken') instead of metadata.version. Cache the directory listing in CustomTokenizerManager.
fix_notes: Do NOT replace version('tiktoken') with importlib.util.find_spec('tiktoken'). tldw_chatbook/__init__.py:25 installs Utils/tiktoken_runtime.py's _TiktokenRuntimeArmingFinder at sys.meta_path[0]. Its find_spec('tiktoken') removes the finder from meta_path (:226) and restores it only on failure or a None spec. A find_spec probe would therefore consume the one-shot finder: the later real `import tiktoken` would skip install_tiktoken_runtime(), which breaks the offline bundled-encodings guarantee. That is exactly what the TASK-24305 comment at token_counter.py:34-41 warns about. Leave the ~1.5 ms version() call alone. The `tokenizers` half is safe: set TOKENIZERS_AVAILABLE from find_spec('tokenizers') and import Tokenizer locally in load_tokenizer (~:136/:160) and install_tokenizer (~:411). Wrap that local import in try/except ImportError, because find_spec cannot prove the native extension loads. Skip the listdir cache (memoised, and only relevant for opt-in users).
evidence:

    from tokenizers import Tokenizer      # module scope, boot path via token_counter
    TOKENIZERS_AVAILABLE = True
token_counter.py:47  version("tiktoken")   # importlib.metadata scan at import
custom_tokenizers.py:204/214  for tokenizer_name in os.listdir(self.tokenizers_dir):   # per estimate miss when mappings exist
reason: Code is as quoted on 840ed2ca58: custom_tokenizers.py:26 imports `tokenizers` at module scope, token_counter.py:47 calls `version("tiktoken")`, and the listdir loops are at :204 and :214. The boot importtime captures (scratch/boot-import/importtime_1/2.txt) show `tokenizers` imported first and only under custom_tokenizers (cumulative 3.7 ms and 11.9 ms in two runs), under token_counter, under Chat.console_display_state. Both modules are in Tests/Performance/boot_budget_snapshots/boot_import_modules.txt. No open task covers this. TASK-24305 is Done and deliberately swapped `import tiktoken` for `version()`. The listdir part is negligible and should be dropped. It only runs when custom_tokenizers_available() is true (the user installed mappings.json), and estimate_tokens memoises every result in _ESTIMATE_CACHE keyed on (model, provider, len, hash), so it runs once per new text, not per estimate.

title: The shared HTTP client factories rebuild a TLS context and re-read the certificate bundle for every new client (9 ms each), and a custom CA also rebuilds or re-hashes it on every call
trigger: Each new httpx client that uses the default verify=True. The on-loop sites are user-initiated and once-per-action (setup-card discovery, the settings-modal model probe). The per-request image-gen clients and per-agent-turn gateway clients run in worker threads. The custom-CA overhead only applies when [network] ssl_verify is a path.
cost: Re-measured in the isolated scratch env: httpx.AsyncClient() median 9.88 ms (max 189 ms), versus 0.04 ms with a shared SSLContext. ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where()) alone is 9.12 ms. This matches the finder. It is real per construction, but it lands on cold or off-loop paths.
fix: Cache one ssl.SSLContext per normalised ssl_verify value (functools.lru_cache keyed on the setting string) and return it from httpx_verify() and ssl_context_for_transport() even for the default True case. Cache the merged-bundle path per (certifi mtime/size, CA digest). In guarded_fetch_requests, default to a module-level pooled session built with create_default_session().
fix_notes: Caching one ssl.SSLContext per normalised setting is fine: httpx accepts a shared context and SSLContext is safe to share across clients and threads. For the custom-CA case, key the cache on (path, mtime_ns, size) or on the content digest, not the path string alone, or a rotated corporate CA stays trusted until restart. The merged-bundle code already guards against exactly this (qodo #2223 finding 7). The module-level pooled requests session for guarded_fetch_requests is NOT low risk. requests.Session is not documented as thread-safe, and its cookie jar would carry cookies across unrelated fetches from different callers and threads, which undermines the function's cross-origin credential-stripping intent. Its verify value would also be frozen at creation. Prefer a per-call egress.create_default_session(): the cost is irrelevant next to the network round-trip, and it also closes a real policy gap, because today's bare requests.Session() ignores the [network] ssl_verify custom CA.
evidence:
def httpx_verify():
    setting = tls_verify_setting()
    if setting is True or setting is False:
        return setting          # True -> httpx builds a fresh SSLContext + certifi load per client
_additive_context: ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where()); load_verify_locations(custom)
_merged_bundle_path: cache_dir = Path(get_user_data_dir()) / "cache"   # F1 cost + sha256 per call
egress.py:1062  sess = session or requests.Session()   # 6 of 9 callers pass no session
reason: Code is as quoted: tls_trust.py:234-244 httpx_verify returns bare True/False, :129-135 _additive_context builds a certifi+custom context on every call, :170-201 _merged_bundle_path does get_user_data_dir, mkdir, stat and a sha256 of the custom CA on every requests_verify(), and egress.py:1062 has `sess = session or requests.Session()`. I traced all 23 factory call sites. None is a hot path on the event loop. (1) Console setup-card discovery (chat_screen.py:15443 run_worker of an async coroutine, so it is on the loop) runs once per screen, only while the setup card blocks, and uses one shared client for the whole gather. (2) console_settings_modal.py:943 probe runs on the loop once per user click. (3) Image_Generation/http_client.fetch_json/create_client builds a client per request inside the sync adapters, which run in worker threads. (4) console_provider_gateway._new_owned_http_client caches one client per loop; agent turns run on a fresh asyncio.run loop in a worker thread, so that is one client per turn off the loop. (5) TTS/base_backends builds one client per backend init. requests_verify() only costs anything with a custom CA, which is a rare config, and those WebSearch callers are sync requests running off the loop. No open task found.

title: optional_deps.check_dependency says it caches but never reads its cache: every call re-imports, logs debug, and for missing modules re-scans sys.path
trigger: Per image preview render, per Markdown parser-factory construction, per Kokoro language check. All are user-driven and none is per-keystroke or per-tick.
cost: Not re-measured. The finder's figures (6.2 us installed, 42.2 us missing) are plausible: __import__ of an already-imported module is a sys.modules hit, the f-string dominates, and a missing module re-walks the sys.path finders. Negligible.
fix: Return DEPENDENCIES_AVAILABLE[feature_name] / MODULES[module_name] when a previous probe has already set them; keep reset_dependency_checks() as the invalidation hook.
fix_notes: The proposed fix is incorrect. (1) DEPENDENCIES_AVAILABLE is pre-seeded with False for pristine keys ('pillow', 'textual_image', 'lxml', 'PIL', ...; _INITIAL_DEPENDENCIES_AVAILABLE at ~:79), so 'already probed' cannot be told apart from 'never probed'. (2) feature_name keys are shared across modules: check_websearch_deps probes lxml, bs4, trafilatura and langdetect all under 'websearch_core', and kokoro_languages uses f'kokoro_{extra}'. Returning DEPENDENCIES_AVAILABLE[feature_name] would report bs4 present just because lxml was. (3) The module deliberately re-probes on False instead of trusting a stale negative (lazy_embeddings_rag_available docstring, ~:905-935), so caching negatives would hide runtime installs. A safe minimal version is a positive-only cache keyed by module: `if module_name in MODULES: DEPENDENCIES_AVAILABLE[feature_name] = True; return True`, and/or brace-style lazy loguru formatting. The gain is about 5 us per call, so this is optional.
evidence:
def check_dependency(module_name, feature_name=None) -> bool:
    """Check if a dependency is available and cache the result."""
    ...
    module = __import__(module_name)
    MODULES[module_name] = module
    logger.debug(f"✅ {module_name} dependency found. ...")
reason: Code is as quoted: optional_deps.py:613 check_dependency writes DEPENDENCIES_AVAILABLE/MODULES but never reads them, and re-runs __import__ (:639) plus an eagerly formatted logger.debug f-string on every call, despite the docstring's 'cache the result'. The callers are as claimed: library_media_image_preview.py:132/:226 (per preview), markdown_parsing.py:98 front_matter_parser_factory (4 call sites), kokoro_languages.py:73, reranker.py:976, search_backend_settings.py:242, terminal_utils.py:62 and others (70 call sites total, most inside optional_deps' own group checkers). The cost is microseconds next to the image decode or Markdown construction it accompanies, so this is hygiene only.

title: The input validation module builds about 30 validation models (pydantic) and loads the regex package at import, on the boot path
trigger: Every boot: tldw_chatbook.app imports Utils.input_validation directly (app.py:95). It is also in boot_import_modules.txt.

title: The durable-write primitives flush to disk twice per write (F_FULLFSYNC on file and directory), costing 4.5–8 ms median and up to 45 ms, which is about 47× a plain fsync
trigger: Every atomic_write_* / atomic_private_write_* call: config saves (mostly threaded; on the loop in lab_frame.toggle_lab_rail per click and in the one-shot apply-detected-local-server), the scheduler heartbeat every 30 s off the loop, and MCP log rotation every 500 records.

fix_notes: A `durable=False` parameter reverses a deliberate durability decision (the TASK-32896 work stream and file_durability's cost note), and config.toml holds credentials and settings, so it is an owner/ADR call, not a low-risk tweak. The lazier fix that keeps durability: move the remaining on-loop writers (lab_frame.toggle_lab_rail -> save_rail_layout, and _apply_detected_local_server) onto thread workers like every other rail or preference save already does. The 'never on the event loop' assertion is TASK-2834's scope (open), so fold it in there rather than filing it again.

title: Warm load_settings()/get_user_data_dir() still pay the per-call storage-admission handshake (TASK-32804.1 fastpath covers only get_cli_setting)
trigger: Every warm load_settings / get_cli_providers_and_models / get_runtime_config_snapshot / get_user_data_dir / get_*_db_path call from the event loop. In this slice: CompactModelBar compose and on_mount (once per ChatScreen instance), and maybe_offer_project_skills_import (app.py:15573, workspace.py:5206/5220/5237, library/settings screens), which calls get_user_data_dir on the loop when there are discoveries. The repo-wide call-site counts make many more loop callers near-certain.

Add a lock-free warm pre-check ahead of the guard for load_settings (return _SETTINGS_CACHE when the source, _CONFIG_GENERATION and the external-edit check are unchanged), and memoize get_user_data_dir/get_model_cache_dir keyed on current_config_identity(). Like the 32804.1 fastpath, this bypasses the ADR-126 pause check (storage._pause, RecoveryRequired) on warm reads; that trade-off is already accepted for get_cli_setting, but say so in the ADR/tests. get_user_data_dir is riskier: memoizing skips secure_private_directory(create=True) and verify_trusted_directory re-verification. A directory deleted or swapped at runtime would then go unnoticed, which weakens a security/TOCTOU posture. Key the memo on config identity plus paths.data_dir plus users_name, and keep re-verification on the DB-open side. The existing verified_user_data_directory() fast path is itself called inside the guard, which is why it does not help today. Pin warm costs in Tests/test_config_warm_read_no_handshake_task32804.py.

title: llama.cpp snapshot manager runs a 1 Hz layout-refreshing tick even when no operation is in flight
trigger: From the first selection of the llama.cpp view in the LLM management window until the window unmounts, the timer fires every second regardless of whether an operation is running. The layout pass happens only while that screen is current.
cost: Estimated well under 1 ms per second: one wakeup, a bounded view() build, one query_one, re-visualizing a short string and a partial layout. That is hygiene-level idle cost, not a measurable percentage of a core.
fix: Arm the interval only while view.started_at is set (start it from _paint when an operation begins, stop it when it ends); skip the update when the text is unchanged; use update(..., layout=False).
fix_notes: Start the interval in _paint or _paint_elapsed when view.started_at becomes non-None, and stop it and set it to None when started_at returns to None. Paint the final status once on the transition so the elapsed suffix disappears. Also skip the Static.update when the composed text equals the last painted text. layout=False is only safe if #snapshot-operation-status has a fixed height. It is a plain Static whose content length varies with the status message and may wrap at narrow widths, so keep layout=True unless the CSS pins its height. The dedupe alone removes most of the idle cost.
evidence:
self._elapsed_timer = self.set_interval(1, self._paint_elapsed)
...
def _paint_elapsed(self):
    view = self.service.view()
    elapsed = "" if view.started_at is None else f" · {int(...)}s"
    self.query_one("#snapshot-operation-status", Static).update(status + elapsed)  # layout=True default
reason: The code matches the finding. llamacpp_snapshot_manager.py:141 on_mount calls self._elapsed_timer = self.set_interval(1, self._paint_elapsed) unconditionally. The timer is stopped only in on_unmount (:153). _paint_elapsed (:198-214) runs service.view() on every tick. view() is O(catalog records) with compatibility_matches per record (snapshot_service.py:473). Each tick also does a query_one and Static.update(status + elapsed) with the default layout=True. In Textual 8.2.8, Static.update (textual/widgets/_static.py:85-95) has no unchanged-content short-circuit: it re-visualizes and calls refresh(layout=True). Widget._check_refresh then posts messages.Layout to the screen, and Screen._on_timer_update runs _refresh_layout while the screen is current. So an idle page pays a 1 Hz wakeup, a view build, a re-visualize and a partial layout pass even when view.started_at is None and the text is identical. The interval is only needed while an operation is in flight: started_at is set at snapshot_service.py:297 and cleared at :427 and :463. Subscribers already get _paint on state changes (service.subscribe(self._paint), and _paint calls _paint_elapsed), so arming the timer on demand is feasible. The widget's own request_refresh docstring says 'never poll on a timer'. The manager is yielded inside the lazy llama-cpp pane (LLM_Management_Window.py:1201-1205, _LazyServerPane), so the timer starts on the first llama.cpp view selection and then persists for the pane's life, including while other provider views are shown. title: Every outermost ChaChaNotes transaction() now pays a ~7-12 ms storage-admission handshake (cross-cutting root of F1/F2/F3/F6/F7; outside the slice)
trigger: Every outermost `with db.transaction()` on the app's file-backed ChaChaNotes DB, on any thread. Confirmed on-loop instances: the Console send snapshot (F1, via prompt_queue._stage_normal_chain -> launch_chain -> _admit_console_turn_to_runtime) and the persona-scope paths. Off-loop but always-on: the 1 Hz legacy trace maintenance run_batch.
cost: Measured (isolated scratch profile, same startup-lease state as the app). transaction()+SELECT 1: median 8.5-9.7 ms, p95 ~20-40 ms, min 4.5 ms. Raw connection: 0.013 ms. execute_query: 0.016 ms. That is ~600x. Outer plus 5 nested: 12.1 ms, so each nested adds ~0.7 ms. Depth scan with the bootstrap root 13 vs 19 components: opens 245 -> 341 (16 per component), median +0.31 ms per component. Extrapolated to a real ~5-component home: ~115 opens and ~3-7 ms per outermost transaction. Still ~300-500x the TASK-31502 figure of 23 us.
fix: Make admission a per-session or per-thread lease that is acquired once and revalidated only on pause, maintenance or generation-change events. The uncontended path of `_core_operation` should be a flag check, like the TASK-31502 AC for the quiescence registry. At minimum, skip `acquire_storage` for read-only transactions and for callers already inside an operation. Slice-local mitigations are F1/F7: use `execute_query` for reads.
fix_notes: Treat the fix as high risk and a design decision for the backup owner. TASK-32562's notes record deliberate 'no cached authority / no validation cache' choices, so a per-session lease reverses a stated design and needs sign-off. Do not skip admission for 'read-only' transaction() blocks. transaction() is used for read-then-write and immediate=True paths, and a read during capture or restore can observe a file being replaced. The safer equivalents are: (a) route pure reads through execute_query/get_connection, which already enforce the pause via _core_access; (b) cut the per-acquire syscall work, e.g. cache the verified directory identity (st_dev/st_ino) of the bootstrap root and registry, revalidated on a generation counter bumped by pause, enroll or maintenance, rather than re-walking every path component 10x per acquire. Nested reuse already exists; do not re-add it. Also add this as new evidence on TASK-31501: its 1 Hz tick went from ~23 us to ~5-9 ms.

self._maintenance_context.__enter__()
# storage_admission.py:163 (_repository_operation)
operation.lease = acquire_storage(operation.path)   # startup_permission + qualified_for + admission_authority + _scope
# cProfile: 50 world-book reads -> 12,250 posix.open calls

Each acquire still re-runs startup_permission x2, qualified_for, admission_authority and _scope x2, and those re-read bootstrap records/registry through _open_verified_parent path walks: 245 posix.open plus ~250 fstat per transaction. title: Image viewer builds the full-screen mosaic synchronously in on_mount

async def on_mount(self):
    widget = self._build_full_size_widget()
...
from ...Utils.mosaic_render import mosaic_from_image
mosaic = mosaic_from_image(self._image, cols, lines)   # cols = app width-8, lines = height-6

title: Character context runs an always-on 2 Hz poll that rebuilds a progress dict per row and never pauses while the reusable Console is suspended
trigger: The timer fires at 2 Hz on the event loop for the life of the reusable ChatScreen, including while another tab is active. The per-row counts rebuild only happens when rows exist and the scope fingerprint and authority guards pass, i.e. once the user has character conversations listed. With no rows, a tick costs one small subtree query.
cost: Estimated, not measured. Rows are bounded by CONSOLE_CHARACTER_GROUP_LIMIT=4 x ROW_LIMIT=5, so up to about 20 rows, not the 5-8 claimed (the search view caps at 8). Each rebuild is dict and list work over live sessions, around 10-50 us. That is at most about 1 ms per tick and well under 0.2% of a core, plus 2 permanent wakeups/s. Hygiene only.
fix: Compute the progress dict once per tick (hoist _progress_counts() out of the row loop / pass it in), skip when not self.screen.is_active, or better make it push-based from the fleet MessageStore inbox change; pause in ChatScreen.on_screen_suspend alongside the other visit timers.
fix_notes: Hoisting the counts fetch out of the row loop is safe, but keep pending_progress_count's per-row scope/database-identity/data-authority guard: pass the precomputed dict in rather than dropping the guard. An early return on `not self.screen.is_current` is cheap and safe, since counts refresh within 0.5 s of resume. Stopping and re-arming the timer from ChatScreen.on_screen_suspend/on_screen_resume also works, but needs a handle to the widget's timer. Making it push-based from MessageStore inbox changes is the better long-term shape but is larger scope.
reason: The code matches at pin 840ed2ca58. console_character_context.py:131 is `self.set_interval(0.5, self._sync_progress_counts)` in on_mount, and the tick walks `self.query(CharacterConversationButton)` and calls `controller.pending_progress_count(row)` once per row. character_context.py:214-230 calls `self._progress_counts()` per row after the scope/authority guards. That goes to wiring.py:1166 `_character_progress_counts`, which calls `screen._ensure_console_agent_bridge()` (cached after the first call), then `bridge.progress_counts()` (MessageStore.pending_counts under a lock, plus a store.progress_owner_ids dict build), then loops `store.sessions()`. So a full counts dict is rebuilt for every visible row on every tick. The widget is composed whenever the character-context controller exists (left_rail.py:2237). The chat route is `reusable=True` (screen_registry.py:84-97), so the screen is suspended, not unmounted. Textual 8.2.8 `Screen._on_screen_suspend` only adds a CSS class, clears the tooltip and bumps stack_updates, and `Timer._run/_tick` invoke the callback regardless of screen state. ChatScreen.on_screen_suspend (chat_screen.py:23578-23667) stops the transcript sync, survivor, cost-TTL and draft-spend timers, but not this one. No backlog task mentions `_sync_progress_counts` or `pending_progress_count`. P3 is the right severity: the cost is tiny and there is no user-visible stall.

title: Expression avatar ticks at 30 Hz and re-renders each frame's mosaic every loop cycle; activity elapsed timers tick at 10 Hz (documented as 1 Hz)
corrected: tldw_chatbook/Widgets/Console/character_expression_avatar.py:142; tldw_chatbook/Widgets/Console/character_expression_avatar.py:216; tldw_chatbook/Widgets/Console/character_expression_avatar.py:232; tldw_chatbook/Widgets/Console/console_assistant_turn.py:220 (stale comment only); sibling 0.1 s ticker at tldw_chatbook/Widgets/Console/console_transcript.py:1544
trigger: Needs a character with a multi-frame animated expression asset (for example Petdex or buddy pets) shown in the Console rail with motion enabled. After that, 30 Hz ticks run for the life of the reusable ChatScreen, including on other tabs, until the avatar is replaced or unmounted. Frames are re-rendered off-loop while the avatar is visible. The 10 Hz elapsed ticks run only while an activity is in the running/stopping state.
cost: Measured under an isolated profile against the audit tree with a random-noise image (the worst case for run merging): mosaic_from_image median 0.483 ms at 24x12 and 1.343 ms at 40x20, which reproduces the finder's numbers. At typical 7-15 fps that is about 0.3-2% of a core in a worker thread, which still contends for the GIL, plus the on-loop Static.update render per frame, for as long as the avatar is visible. Hidden 30 Hz ticks are a few attribute checks each: a wakeup tax, not CPU. P3 fits because the cost is conditional on a niche feature and each tick is well under 10 ms.
fix: Cache rendered mosaics per frame index in PreparedExpression (render each frame once), pause the avatar timer instead of early-returning when not visible (resume via on_screen_resume / visibility), and set _RAW_CLI_ELAPSED_TICK_SECONDS to 1.0 with whole-second copy (or keep .1f but only while on screen).
fix_notes: Per-frame mosaic caching needs a memory cap. Frames go up to MAX_EXPRESSION_FRAME_COUNT=512, a 40x20 styled Text is roughly 100 KB or more, and _preparation_bytes does not account for renderables. Cache only under a byte or frame budget, per widget instance; box and monochrome are fixed per instance, so no extra invalidation is needed. Widgets do not receive ScreenSuspend/ScreenResume. To pause the timer while hidden, either stop it on `not self.screen.is_current` and re-arm from ChatScreen.on_screen_resume via a hook, or just drop to a slow cadence while not visible. A naive stop with no resume path would freeze the animation for good. Changing the elapsed ticker to 1 Hz is a UX and copy change that breaks pinned tests. Recommend only fixing the stale 'Once-per-second' comment.
evidence:
self._timer = self.set_interval(1 / 30, self._tick)   # infinite for plays == 0 (frame_at)
# _tick -> _visible() does screen.get_widget_at(region.center) every tick
# _paint(index) -> asyncio.to_thread(render_character_avatar_mosaic, image, ...) on every frame change, no per-frame cache
_RAW_CLI_ELAPSED_TICK_SECONDS = 0.1
# comment in _tick_raw_cli_elapsed: 'Once-per-second elapsed repaint'
reason: character_expression_avatar.py:142 arms `set_interval(1 / 30, self._tick)` only when the prepared expression has more than one frame. `_tick` (232-257) stops the timer only when `_current()` goes false or when `frame_at` reports finished. `frame_at` never reports finished when plays == 0, i.e. a WebP/GIF with loop=0 (character_expression_playback.py:69-83, 166-173). A plays=1 asset hidden mid-play also never advances elapsed time, so it keeps ticking too. While the Console is suspended, `_is_current` is still true: it checks `request == _latest_built_request and _is_mounted()` (character.py:445), and the screen stays mounted. `_visible()` then returns early on `self.screen.is_current`, so a hidden tick is cheap but still a wakeup, 30 per second. When visible, every tick also calls `screen.get_widget_at(region.center)`. On each frame change, `_paint` dispatches `asyncio.to_thread(render_character_avatar_mosaic, ...)` and there is no per-frame renderable cache, so every loop of the animation re-renders every frame. That path only applies in pixels mode, which is the default (`_console_image_default_mode() or 'pixels'`); graphics mode just swaps `_graphics.image`. The avatar only animates when `expression_motion_enabled` holds: Dynamic mode, react or manual, animations_enabled, and not reduce_motion. The elapsed-timer sub-claim is weak. `_RAW_CLI_ELAPSED_TICK_SECONDS = 0.1` (console_assistant_turn.py:28) is deliberate: the copy is formatted `{elapsed:.1f}s` (lines 61 and 90), and tests pin tenths (Tests/UI/test_console_raw_cli_transcript.py:964 `"Running · 0.5s"`). Only the 'Once-per-second' comment at line 220 is stale. Each tick is a single `layout=False` update of a one-row Static, and the timer runs only while a tool or raw CLI command is running. TASK-32023 (Done) introduced the playback. No open task covers this.
